toyota.name: Toyota
toyota.description: Toyota is the world's largest automaker by volume, renowned for reliability and resale value. Founded in Japan, Toyota pioneered hybrid technology with the Prius and continues to lead in quality and durability. The brand offers everything from economical sedans to rugged trucks and luxury vehicles through its Lexus division.

honda.name: Honda
honda.description: Honda is one of the most trusted automotive brands in America, known for engineering excellence and long-term reliability. The Civic and Accord are perennial best-sellers that set the standard for compact and midsize sedans. Honda also produces motorcycles, power equipment, and aircraft.

ford.name: Ford
ford.description: Ford Motor Company is an American icon and the creator of the modern assembly line. The F-150 has been America's best-selling truck for over four decades, and the Mustang is one of the most recognized sports cars in history. Ford is aggressively expanding into electric vehicles with the Mustang Mach-E and F-150 Lightning.

chevrolet.name: Chevrolet
chevrolet.description: Chevrolet is one of America's most popular and enduring automotive brands, offering a full lineup from compact cars to heavy-duty trucks. The Silverado competes head-to-head with Ford's F-150, while the Corvette is an American performance legend. Chevrolet is a division of General Motors and sells vehicles in over 100 countries.

bmw.name: BMW
bmw.description: BMW, short for Bayerische Motoren Werke, is a German luxury automaker synonymous with driving pleasure and precision engineering. The brand's tagline 'The Ultimate Driving Machine' reflects its commitment to performance-oriented luxury vehicles. BMW offers a complete range of sedans, SUVs, coupes, and an expanding lineup of electric i-series models.

mercedes-benz.name: Mercedes-Benz
mercedes-benz.description: Mercedes-Benz is the world's oldest automotive brand, tracing its lineage to Karl Benz's 1886 Patent-Motorwagen. Known for cutting-edge technology, safety innovations, and refined luxury, Mercedes sets the standard for premium automobiles. The brand spans from entry-level luxury to ultra-premium Maybach models and high-performance AMG variants.

audi.name: Audi
audi.description: Audi is a German luxury automaker owned by the Volkswagen Group, known for its quattro all-wheel-drive system and progressive design language. The brand combines cutting-edge technology with understated elegance across its sedan and SUV lineups. Audi's e-tron electric vehicles represent the brand's push toward sustainable luxury mobility.

nissan.name: Nissan
nissan.description: Nissan is a Japanese automaker that offers a broad range of affordable and reliable vehicles for the American market. The Rogue is one of the best-selling SUVs in the country, and the Altima remains a popular midsize sedan. Nissan was an early pioneer in mass-market electric vehicles with the Leaf.

hyundai.name: Hyundai
hyundai.description: Hyundai has transformed from a budget brand into a formidable competitor offering exceptional value, technology, and design. The South Korean automaker backs its vehicles with one of the best warranties in the industry at 10 years or 100,000 miles on the powertrain. Hyundai's IONIQ sub-brand is rapidly expanding in the electric vehicle market.

kia.name: Kia
kia.description: Kia has undergone a dramatic brand transformation, evolving from a value brand into a design-forward automaker with award-winning vehicles. The Telluride has won numerous SUV of the Year awards, and the EV6 represents Kia's ambitious electric future. Kia offers a 10-year, 100,000-mile powertrain warranty, among the best in the industry.

volkswagen.name: Volkswagen
volkswagen.description: Volkswagen is one of the world's largest automakers, known for German engineering at accessible price points. The brand's name translates to 'People's Car,' reflecting its mission to offer quality vehicles for everyday drivers. VW is investing heavily in electrification with the ID series of electric vehicles.

subaru.name: Subaru
subaru.description: Subaru is known for its standard symmetrical all-wheel drive, boxer engines, and loyal customer base. The brand has a strong following among outdoor enthusiasts and is consistently ranked among the safest vehicles on the road. Subaru's commitment to safety and all-weather capability makes it especially popular in northern and mountainous states.

mazda.name: Mazda
mazda.description: Mazda is a Japanese automaker that prioritizes driving dynamics and design, often described as offering premium experiences at mainstream prices. The MX-5 Miata is the best-selling roadster in history, and the CX-5 is one of the top-rated compact SUVs. Mazda's Skyactiv technology focuses on efficiency without sacrificing performance.

lexus.name: Lexus
lexus.description: Lexus is Toyota's luxury division and has become synonymous with refined comfort, whisper-quiet cabins, and legendary reliability. The RX was one of the first luxury crossover SUVs and remains a segment leader. Lexus consistently tops customer satisfaction and dependability surveys.

acura.name: Acura
acura.description: Acura is Honda's luxury and performance division, offering precision-crafted vehicles with a sportier edge than many luxury competitors. The MDX is one of the best-selling three-row luxury SUVs in America. Acura combines Honda's renowned reliability with premium materials and advanced technology.

infiniti.name: Infiniti
infiniti.description: Infiniti is Nissan's luxury brand, offering a lineup of performance-inspired sedans and SUVs with distinctive design. The brand is known for powerful VQ-series engines and driver-focused interiors. Infiniti competes in the entry and mid-luxury segments against Lexus, Acura, and German rivals.

volvo.name: Volvo
volvo.description: Volvo is a Swedish luxury automaker with an unmatched reputation for safety innovation, having invented the three-point seatbelt in 1959. Now owned by Geely, Volvo combines Scandinavian minimalist design with cutting-edge safety technology. The brand has committed to becoming fully electric by 2030.

jeep.name: Jeep
jeep.description: Jeep is an iconic American brand synonymous with off-road capability and rugged adventure. The Wrangler traces its lineage to the World War II military vehicle and remains the gold standard for off-road SUVs. Jeep is a division of Stellantis and offers vehicles ranging from compact crossovers to full-size luxury SUVs.

ram.name: Ram
ram.description: Ram Trucks was spun off from Dodge in 2010 to create a dedicated truck brand under what is now Stellantis. The Ram 1500 is widely praised for its luxurious interior, smooth ride, and innovative features like the multifunction tailgate. Ram has rapidly gained market share in the fiercely competitive full-size truck segment.

dodge.name: Dodge
dodge.description: Dodge is an American performance brand known for muscle cars and powerful engines, especially the legendary Hemi V8. The Charger and Challenger are modern muscle car icons, and the Durango offers SUV practicality with performance credentials. Dodge is transitioning toward electrified performance under Stellantis.

chrysler.name: Chrysler
chrysler.description: Chrysler is one of America's oldest automotive brands, now operating as a smaller division within Stellantis. The Pacifica is widely regarded as the best minivan on the market, offering a plug-in hybrid option. Chrysler is being repositioned as a technology-forward brand with plans for full electrification.

buick.name: Buick
buick.description: Buick is a General Motors brand that bridges the gap between mainstream and luxury, offering quiet and comfortable vehicles at accessible prices. The brand is one of the oldest in America and has a massive following in China. Buick has shifted to an all-SUV lineup in the US market.

gmc.name: GMC
gmc.description: GMC is General Motors' premium truck and SUV brand, offering upscale versions of Chevrolet's truck lineup with distinctive styling and additional features. The Sierra and Yukon are among the most popular full-size trucks and SUVs in America. GMC revived the Hummer nameplate as an all-electric supertruck.

cadillac.name: Cadillac
cadillac.description: Cadillac is General Motors' luxury brand and was once the undisputed standard of the world in American luxury automobiles. The Escalade remains an icon of American luxury, and Cadillac is reinventing itself with the all-electric Lyriq. The brand competes with BMW, Mercedes-Benz, and Lexus in the premium market.

lincoln.name: Lincoln
lincoln.description: Lincoln is Ford's luxury division, known for serene interiors, smooth rides, and the iconic Navigator full-size SUV. The brand has undergone a significant renaissance with modern designs and the 'Quiet Flight' philosophy. Lincoln competes in the American luxury market against Cadillac, Lexus, and European imports.

tesla.name: Tesla
tesla.description: Tesla revolutionized the automotive industry by proving that electric vehicles could be desirable, high-performance, and practical for everyday use. The Model Y and Model 3 are among the best-selling vehicles in the world, and Tesla's Supercharger network is the largest fast-charging network in North America. Tesla also develops autonomous driving technology, energy storage, and solar products.

rivian.name: Rivian
rivian.description: Rivian is an American electric vehicle startup that launched with the R1T, the first electric pickup truck to reach production. The R1S is a three-row electric SUV that competes with luxury offerings from traditional automakers. Rivian also builds electric delivery vans for Amazon.

lucid.name: Lucid
lucid.description: Lucid Motors is an American electric vehicle manufacturer that produces the Lucid Air, an ultra-luxury EV sedan with industry-leading range. The Air Grand Touring achieved an EPA-estimated 516 miles of range, the highest of any EV. Lucid is backed by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and is expanding into the SUV market with the Gravity.

porsche.name: Porsche
porsche.description: Porsche is a German sports car manufacturer and one of the most profitable automakers in the world. The 911 is one of the most iconic sports cars ever made, while the Cayenne and Macan SUVs drive the brand's sales volume. Porsche has successfully entered the electric market with the Taycan.

land-rover.name: Land Rover
land-rover.description: Land Rover is a British luxury SUV brand known for combining opulent interiors with genuine off-road capability. The Range Rover is the definitive luxury SUV and has been favored by royalty and celebrities for decades. Land Rover is owned by Tata Motors' Jaguar Land Rover division.

jaguar.name: Jaguar
jaguar.description: Jaguar is a British luxury automaker with a heritage rooted in elegant sports cars like the E-Type and XK series. The brand has expanded into SUVs with the F-Pace while maintaining its sporting character. Jaguar is transitioning to an all-electric luxury brand under Jaguar Land Rover.

mitsubishi.name: Mitsubishi
mitsubishi.description: Mitsubishi is a Japanese automaker now partnered with the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance, offering affordable SUVs and crossovers. The Outlander is available as a plug-in hybrid, one of the most affordable PHEVs on the market. Mitsubishi is known for value pricing and generous warranty coverage.

genesis.name: Genesis
genesis.description: Genesis is Hyundai's luxury brand that has rapidly established itself as a serious competitor to established German and Japanese luxury marques. The brand offers elegant design, advanced technology, and exceptional value compared to BMW and Mercedes-Benz. Genesis includes complimentary scheduled maintenance and valet service for owners.

alfa-romeo.name: Alfa Romeo
alfa-romeo.description: Alfa Romeo is an Italian luxury automaker with a storied racing heritage dating back over a century. The Giulia sedan and Stelvio SUV offer passionate Italian design and engaging driving dynamics. Alfa Romeo is part of Stellantis and is expanding its lineup with new electrified models.

fiat.name: Fiat
fiat.description: Fiat is Italy's largest automaker and one of the founding brands of Stellantis. The Fiat 500 is an iconic city car known for its retro charm and compact dimensions. Fiat's US presence has been scaled back significantly, with the brand focusing on the electrified 500e.

mini.name: Mini
mini.description: Mini is a British brand owned by BMW, known for its iconic compact cars with go-kart-like handling and distinctive retro-modern design. The Cooper is available in hardtop, convertible, and performance JCW variants. Mini is expanding into electric vehicles with the Cooper SE.

saab.name: Saab
saab.description: Saab was a Swedish automaker known for quirky engineering, turbocharged performance, and aviation-inspired design. The brand had a devoted following but ceased production in 2011 after bankruptcy. Saab vehicles were known for their unique ignition placement between the seats and strong safety record.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.description: Saturn was a General Motors brand created to compete with Japanese imports through a no-haggle pricing model and polymer body panels. The brand cultivated an enthusiastic owner community with annual 'Homecoming' events at its Spring Hill, Tennessee factory. Saturn was discontinued in 2010 during GM's bankruptcy restructuring.

pontiac.name: Pontiac
pontiac.description: Pontiac was General Motors' performance-oriented brand, famous for the GTO, Firebird, and Trans Am muscle cars. The brand's tagline 'We Build Excitement' captured its sporty image throughout the 1980s and 1990s. Pontiac was discontinued in 2010 as part of GM's bankruptcy restructuring.

oldsmobile.name: Oldsmobile
oldsmobile.description: Oldsmobile was one of America's oldest automotive brands and a cornerstone of General Motors for over a century. The Cutlass was America's best-selling car in the 1970s, and the 442 was a legendary muscle car. Oldsmobile was discontinued in 2004 after declining sales and brand identity challenges.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.description: Mercury was Ford's mid-level brand, positioned between Ford and Lincoln, offering slightly upscale versions of Ford vehicles. The Grand Marquis was a staple of taxi fleets and police departments, and the brand had a strong following among traditional American car buyers. Mercury was discontinued in 2011 as Ford streamlined its brand portfolio.

hummer.name: Hummer
hummer.description: Hummer was a brand of large SUVs and trucks derived from the military HMMWV (Humvee). The H2 became a cultural phenomenon in the early 2000s, symbolizing excess and off-road capability. The original Hummer brand was discontinued in 2010, but the nameplate was revived as a GMC sub-brand for an electric supertruck.

plymouth.name: Plymouth
plymouth.description: Plymouth was Chrysler's value brand, known for producing affordable vehicles and iconic muscle cars like the Barracuda and Road Runner. The Plymouth Voyager was one of the original minivans that created the segment in 1984. Plymouth was discontinued in 2001 as Chrysler consolidated its brand lineup.

scion.name: Scion
scion.description: Scion was Toyota's youth-oriented brand, designed to attract younger buyers with affordable, customizable vehicles and a no-haggle pricing model. The tC coupe and xB box car developed cult followings, and the FR-S sports car became a tuner favorite. Scion was discontinued in 2016, with its best models absorbed into the Toyota lineup.

suzuki.name: Suzuki
suzuki.description: Suzuki was a Japanese automaker known for small, affordable vehicles and the legendary Samurai compact SUV. The brand left the US automobile market in 2012 due to low sales volume, though it remains a major global automaker. Suzuki continues to sell motorcycles and ATVs in the United States.

isuzu.name: Isuzu
isuzu.description: Isuzu was known in the US market for rugged SUVs and trucks, particularly the Trooper and Rodeo. The brand exited the US consumer vehicle market in 2009 but continues to sell commercial trucks in North America. Isuzu remains one of the world's largest manufacturers of medium and heavy-duty diesel trucks.

smart.name: Smart
smart.description: Smart was a microcar brand created as a joint venture between Swatch and Mercedes-Benz, producing ultra-compact city cars. The ForTwo was the brand's signature model, measuring under nine feet long and perfect for urban parking. Smart exited the US market in 2019 but continues to sell electric vehicles in Europe and China.

polestar.name: Polestar
polestar.description: Polestar is a Swedish electric vehicle brand spun off from Volvo, focused on performance-oriented EVs with minimalist Scandinavian design. The Polestar 2 is a direct competitor to the Tesla Model 3, offering a refined driving experience and premium materials. Polestar is expanding its lineup with the Polestar 3 SUV and Polestar 4 coupe-SUV.

fisker.name: Fisker
fisker.description: Fisker was an American electric vehicle startup founded by Henrik Fisker, who previously created the Fisker Karma plug-in hybrid. The Fisker Ocean was a mid-size electric SUV that aimed to combine sustainability with accessible pricing. Fisker filed for bankruptcy in 2024 after production and distribution challenges.

lotus.name: Lotus
lotus.description: Lotus is a British sports car manufacturer renowned for lightweight engineering and exceptional handling, following founder Colin Chapman's philosophy of 'simplify, then add lightness.' The Emira is the brand's final internal combustion sports car, while the Eletre marks Lotus's entry into the electric SUV market. Lotus is now owned by Geely and is expanding globally.

maserati.name: Maserati
maserati.description: Maserati is an Italian luxury automaker with a rich racing heritage, known for its distinctive trident logo and sonorous engines. The brand offers grand touring cars and luxury SUVs that blend Italian craftsmanship with sporting character. Maserati is part of Stellantis and is electrifying its lineup with the Folgore range.

aston-martin.name: Aston Martin
aston-martin.description: Aston Martin is a British ultra-luxury sports car maker, famously associated with James Bond and British elegance. The brand produces hand-crafted grand tourers and the DBX luxury SUV at its Gaydon factory. Aston Martin combines bespoke craftsmanship with high performance in a very exclusive package.

bentley.name: Bentley
bentley.description: Bentley is a British ultra-luxury automaker owned by the Volkswagen Group, producing handcrafted vehicles at its Crewe factory in England. The Continental GT is the definitive modern grand tourer, and the Bentayga was the first ultra-luxury SUV. Bentley combines unmatched cabin opulence with surprising performance capabilities.

rolls-royce.name: Rolls-Royce
rolls-royce.description: Rolls-Royce is the pinnacle of automotive luxury, hand-building vehicles at its Goodwood factory with unparalleled attention to detail. Each Rolls-Royce takes months to complete and can be bespoke-ordered to virtually any specification. The brand, owned by BMW, has entered the electric era with the Spectre.

lamborghini.name: Lamborghini
lamborghini.description: Lamborghini is an Italian supercar manufacturer known for dramatic design, screaming engines, and outrageous performance. The Urus super-SUV has become the brand's best-selling model, making Lamborghini more accessible than ever. Lamborghini is owned by the Volkswagen Group through Audi and is transitioning to hybrid powertrains.

ferrari.name: Ferrari
ferrari.description: Ferrari is the world's most iconic sports car brand, synonymous with Formula 1 racing, Italian passion, and automotive excellence. The Prancing Horse badge represents decades of engineering innovation and racing victories. Ferrari deliberately limits production to maintain exclusivity and has become one of the most valuable luxury brands in the world.

mclaren.name: McLaren
mclaren.description: McLaren is a British supercar manufacturer born from the legendary McLaren Formula 1 team. The brand produces lightweight, carbon-fiber supercars that emphasize driver engagement and technological innovation. McLaren's road cars share engineering DNA with its F1 race cars, using carbon fiber tubs and advanced aerodynamics.

bugatti.name: Bugatti
bugatti.description: Bugatti is a French hyper-luxury automaker that produces the fastest and most expensive production cars in the world. The Chiron and its variants can exceed 300 mph, representing the absolute pinnacle of automotive engineering. Bugatti is now part of Bugatti Rimac, a joint venture between Porsche and Croatian EV maker Rimac.

maybach.name: Maybach
maybach.description: Maybach is Mercedes-Benz's ultra-luxury sub-brand, revived in 2015 as Mercedes-Maybach after the standalone brand was discontinued in 2012. The Mercedes-Maybach S-Class represents the pinnacle of luxury sedan motoring, competing with Rolls-Royce and Bentley. Maybach models feature exclusive design elements, premium materials, and extended wheelbases for rear-seat comfort.

delorean.name: DeLorean
delorean.description: DeLorean Motor Company produced the iconic DMC-12, a stainless steel sports car with gull-wing doors that became a pop culture legend through the Back to the Future films. The original company produced fewer than 9,000 cars before going bankrupt in 1982. A new DeLorean Motor Company has announced plans for an electric vehicle revival.

toyota/camry.name: Camry
toyota/camry.description: The Toyota Camry has been America's best-selling sedan for over two decades, offering a balanced combination of comfort, reliability, and fuel efficiency. Known for exceptional resale value and low cost of ownership, the Camry is the benchmark midsize sedan.

toyota/corolla.name: Corolla
toyota/corolla.description: The Toyota Corolla is the best-selling car in history with over 50 million units sold worldwide. Known for bulletproof reliability and low running costs, the Corolla offers practical transportation with modern technology and safety features.

toyota/rav4.name: RAV4
toyota/rav4.description: The Toyota RAV4 is one of the best-selling SUVs in the world, pioneering the compact crossover segment in 1996. Available as a gas model, hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and the sporty RAV4 Prime, it offers versatility for every buyer.

toyota/highlander.name: Highlander
toyota/highlander.description: The Toyota Highlander is a three-row midsize SUV that combines family-friendly space with Toyota reliability. Available with a fuel-efficient hybrid powertrain, the Highlander offers comfortable seating for up to eight passengers.

toyota/tacoma.name: Tacoma
toyota/tacoma.description: The Toyota Tacoma is the best-selling midsize pickup truck in America, prized for its off-road capability and legendary resale value. The TRD Pro trim is one of the most capable factory off-road trucks available.

honda/civic.name: Civic
honda/civic.description: The Honda Civic is one of the most popular compact cars in history, known for excellent fuel efficiency, engaging driving dynamics, and long-term reliability. The Civic Type R is one of the most acclaimed performance hatchbacks available.

honda/accord.name: Accord
honda/accord.description: The Honda Accord is a midsize sedan that consistently earns top marks for quality, value, and driving enjoyment. The Accord has won more Car and Driver 10Best awards than any other vehicle in history.

honda/cr-v.name: CR-V
honda/cr-v.description: The Honda CR-V is one of the best-selling compact SUVs in America, offering a spacious interior, excellent fuel economy, and Honda's reputation for dependability. The CR-V Hybrid adds electric assistance for even better efficiency.

ford/f-150.name: F-150
ford/f-150.description: The Ford F-150 has been America's best-selling vehicle for over 40 consecutive years, offering unmatched versatility from work truck to luxury hauler. The F-150 Lightning brings full-size truck capability to the electric age.

ford/explorer.name: Explorer
ford/explorer.description: The Ford Explorer helped create the SUV boom of the 1990s and remains one of the most popular three-row SUVs in America. The Explorer offers seating for seven with a range of powertrains including a performance ST model.

ford/mustang.name: Mustang
ford/mustang.description: The Ford Mustang is an American icon and the world's best-selling sports car, offering thrilling performance at accessible prices. From the turbocharged EcoBoost to the supercharged GT500, the Mustang delivers excitement for every budget.

chevrolet/silverado.name: Silverado
chevrolet/silverado.description: The Chevrolet Silverado is one of America's best-selling full-size trucks, competing directly with the Ford F-150 and Ram 1500. Available in a wide range of trims from work truck to luxury High Country, the Silverado offers capability for every need.

chevrolet/equinox.name: Equinox
chevrolet/equinox.description: The Chevrolet Equinox is a compact crossover SUV that offers a comfortable ride, good fuel economy, and a competitive price point. The all-electric Equinox EV brings affordable electric transportation to the mainstream market.

bmw/3-series.name: 3 Series
bmw/3-series.description: The BMW 3 Series is the sports sedan benchmark, setting the standard for driving dynamics in the luxury segment for nearly five decades. Available as a sedan and wagon, with rear-wheel and all-wheel drive options.

bmw/x3.name: X3
bmw/x3.description: The BMW X3 is one of the best-selling luxury compact SUVs, offering BMW's trademark driving dynamics in a practical package. The X3 M Competition delivers supercar-rivaling performance in an SUV body.

mercedes-benz/c-class.name: C-Class
mercedes-benz/c-class.description: The Mercedes-Benz C-Class is the entry point to the Mercedes luxury sedan lineup, offering cutting-edge technology, refined comfort, and the prestige of the three-pointed star badge. The AMG C 63 variant delivers explosive performance.

mercedes-benz/gle.name: GLE
mercedes-benz/gle.description: The Mercedes-Benz GLE is a midsize luxury SUV that combines comfort, technology, and capability in a sophisticated package. Available with mild-hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and high-performance AMG powertrains.

audi/a4.name: A4
audi/a4.description: The Audi A4 is a compact luxury sedan known for its refined interior, advanced technology, and available quattro all-wheel drive. The A4 competes with the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes C-Class in the fiercely competitive entry luxury segment.

audi/q5.name: Q5
audi/q5.description: The Audi Q5 is one of the best-selling luxury compact SUVs, offering a premium interior, smooth ride, and Audi's legendary quattro all-wheel-drive system. The Q5 is available in standard, Sportback, and high-performance SQ5 variants.

nissan/altima.name: Altima
nissan/altima.description: The Nissan Altima is a midsize sedan that offers available all-wheel drive, a rarity in the segment, along with good fuel economy and a comfortable cabin. The Altima competes with the Camry, Accord, and Malibu.

nissan/rogue.name: Rogue
nissan/rogue.description: The Nissan Rogue is one of the best-selling compact SUVs in America, offering a spacious interior, excellent fuel economy, and a comprehensive suite of safety technology. The Rogue was completely redesigned with bold styling.

hyundai/elantra.name: Elantra
hyundai/elantra.description: The Hyundai Elantra is a compact sedan that punches above its weight with a stylish design, generous features, and excellent warranty coverage. The Elantra N variant offers genuine sports sedan performance at an accessible price.

hyundai/tucson.name: Tucson
hyundai/tucson.description: The Hyundai Tucson is a compact crossover SUV with bold styling, a premium interior, and available hybrid and plug-in hybrid powertrains. The Tucson offers one of the best value propositions in its class.

hyundai/santa-fe.name: Santa Fe
hyundai/santa-fe.description: The Hyundai Santa Fe is a midsize SUV offering a comfortable ride, generous standard features, and available hybrid and plug-in hybrid powertrains. The Santa Fe provides excellent value with a spacious interior and Hyundai's comprehensive warranty.

hyundai/sonata.name: Sonata
hyundai/sonata.description: The Hyundai Sonata is a midsize sedan known for its striking design, generous features, and excellent value. Available in hybrid and N Line performance variants, the Sonata offers a compelling alternative to traditional segment leaders.

hyundai/kona.name: Kona
hyundai/kona.description: The Hyundai Kona is a subcompact crossover SUV offering distinctive styling, a tech-rich interior, and available all-wheel drive. The Kona Electric variant provides a fully electric option with competitive range.

hyundai/palisade.name: Palisade
hyundai/palisade.description: The Hyundai Palisade is a three-row SUV that elevated Hyundai's brand with premium materials, a refined ride, and a spacious cabin. The Palisade offers near-luxury features at a mainstream price.

hyundai/venue.name: Venue
hyundai/venue.description: The Hyundai Venue is an entry-level subcompact SUV offering an affordable starting price, easy maneuverability, and a surprisingly feature-rich interior for its class.

hyundai/ioniq-5.name: IONIQ 5
hyundai/ioniq-5.description: The Hyundai IONIQ 5 is an all-electric crossover built on Hyundai's dedicated E-GMP platform, featuring ultra-fast 800V charging, a retro-futuristic design, and a spacious flat-floor interior.

kia/sorento.name: Sorento
kia/sorento.description: The Kia Sorento is a midsize SUV offering three rows of seating, available hybrid and plug-in hybrid powertrains, and Kia's industry-leading warranty. The Sorento combines family practicality with attractive design.

kia/telluride.name: Telluride
kia/telluride.description: The Kia Telluride quickly became one of the most acclaimed SUVs in America, winning multiple SUV of the Year awards with its spacious three-row interior, premium feel, and competitive pricing.

kia/sportage.name: Sportage
kia/sportage.description: The Kia Sportage is a compact SUV with bold styling, a tech-forward interior, and available hybrid and plug-in hybrid powertrains. The Sportage offers one of the most distinctive designs in its segment.

kia/forte.name: Forte
kia/forte.description: The Kia Forte is a compact sedan offering excellent value with a generous features list, a comfortable ride, and Kia's industry-leading warranty. Available in sedan and hatchback body styles.

kia/soul.name: Soul
kia/soul.description: The Kia Soul is a distinctive boxy crossover known for its funky styling, spacious interior, and value-oriented pricing. The Soul EV offers an all-electric variant for eco-conscious buyers.

kia/k5.name: K5
kia/k5.description: The Kia K5 replaced the Optima as Kia's midsize sedan, bringing a sportier design, available all-wheel drive, and a turbocharged GT variant with genuine performance credentials.

kia/seltos.name: Seltos
kia/seltos.description: The Kia Seltos is a subcompact SUV slotting between the Soul and Sportage, offering a refined ride, available all-wheel drive, and a well-appointed interior at a competitive price.

kia/ev6.name: EV6
kia/ev6.description: The Kia EV6 is an all-electric crossover built on the E-GMP platform, featuring ultra-fast charging, a striking design, and the high-performance GT variant producing over 576 horsepower.

tesla/model-3.name: Model 3
tesla/model-3.description: The Tesla Model 3 brought electric vehicles to the mainstream market with impressive range, instant acceleration, and access to the Tesla Supercharger network. The Model 3 is one of the best-selling electric vehicles in history.

tesla/model-y.name: Model Y
tesla/model-y.description: The Tesla Model Y is a compact electric SUV that has become one of the best-selling vehicles in the world across all powertrains. Offering impressive range, cargo space, and Tesla's technology ecosystem.

jeep/wrangler.name: Wrangler
jeep/wrangler.description: The Jeep Wrangler is the ultimate off-road SUV, offering removable doors and roof panels, solid axles, and legendary Trail Rated capability. The Wrangler 4xe plug-in hybrid adds electric torque for trail crawling.

jeep/grand-cherokee.name: Grand Cherokee
jeep/grand-cherokee.description: The Jeep Grand Cherokee is a premium midsize SUV that combines genuine off-road capability with on-road luxury. The Grand Cherokee L adds a third row, while the Grand Cherokee 4xe offers plug-in hybrid efficiency.

ram/1500.description: The Ram 1500 is widely praised as having the most refined interior and smoothest ride in the full-size truck segment. The coil-spring rear suspension and available air suspension set it apart from competitors.

subaru/outback.name: Outback
subaru/outback.description: The Subaru Outback is a rugged wagon-SUV crossover with standard all-wheel drive and impressive ground clearance. Popular with outdoor enthusiasts, the Outback offers reliable all-weather capability and excellent visibility.

mazda/cx-5.name: CX-5
mazda/cx-5.description: The Mazda CX-5 is a compact crossover that offers a premium driving experience at mainstream prices, with engaging handling and an upscale interior. The CX-5 consistently earns top ratings for driving dynamics in its class.

lexus/rx.name: RX
lexus/rx.description: The Lexus RX is the best-selling luxury SUV in America, pioneering the luxury crossover segment with its combination of comfort, reliability, and refinement. Available as a hybrid and plug-in hybrid for exceptional fuel efficiency.

volkswagen/jetta.name: Jetta
volkswagen/jetta.description: The Volkswagen Jetta is a compact sedan that offers German engineering and build quality at an accessible price point. The Jetta GLI provides genuine sport sedan performance with an affordable price tag.

volkswagen/tiguan.name: Tiguan
volkswagen/tiguan.description: The Volkswagen Tiguan is a compact SUV that offers European driving dynamics, a spacious interior, and available third-row seating. The Tiguan combines VW's engineering heritage with everyday practicality.

volkswagen/atlas.name: Atlas
volkswagen/atlas.description: The Volkswagen Atlas is a three-row midsize SUV offering one of the most spacious interiors in its class, straightforward technology, and a comfortable ride designed specifically for American families.

volkswagen/taos.name: Taos
volkswagen/taos.description: The Volkswagen Taos is a subcompact SUV offering German engineering at an accessible price, with a roomy interior for its size and available all-wheel drive.

volkswagen/golf.name: Golf
volkswagen/golf.description: The Volkswagen Golf is an iconic hatchback known worldwide for its refined driving dynamics, practical design, and versatility. The Golf GTI and Golf R variants are benchmark hot hatches.

volkswagen/id-4.name: ID.4
volkswagen/id-4.description: The Volkswagen ID.4 is an all-electric compact SUV built on VW's MEB platform, offering a spacious interior, competitive range, and an approachable entry point into electric vehicle ownership.

volkswagen/atlas-cross-sport.name: Atlas Cross Sport
volkswagen/atlas-cross-sport.description: The Volkswagen Atlas Cross Sport is a two-row midsize SUV with a sportier roofline than the standard Atlas, offering a stylish design, generous cargo space, and available V6 power.

porsche/cayenne.name: Cayenne
porsche/cayenne.description: The Porsche Cayenne redefined the luxury performance SUV segment, offering genuine Porsche driving dynamics in a practical five-seat package. Available with twin-turbo V6, V8, and plug-in hybrid powertrains.

porsche/911.description: The Porsche 911 is one of the most iconic sports cars ever made, evolving over six decades while maintaining its distinctive rear-engine layout. From the base Carrera to the track-focused GT3 RS, the 911 offers performance for every enthusiast.

volvo/xc60.name: XC60
volvo/xc60.description: The Volvo XC60 is a compact luxury SUV that prioritizes safety, Scandinavian design, and comfort. Available with mild-hybrid and plug-in hybrid powertrains, the XC60 combines elegance with environmental consciousness.

land-rover/range-rover.name: Range Rover
land-rover/range-rover.description: The Range Rover is the definitive luxury SUV, combining aristocratic elegance with genuine off-road capability. Each generation has advanced the art of luxury motoring, with the latest offering hybrid powertrains and breathtaking refinement.

cadillac/escalade.name: Escalade
cadillac/escalade.description: The Cadillac Escalade is an icon of American luxury, featuring a massive OLED display, Super Cruise hands-free driving, and opulent appointments. The Escalade-V adds supercharged V8 power for performance luxury.

lincoln/navigator.name: Navigator
lincoln/navigator.description: The Lincoln Navigator is a full-size luxury SUV that competes with the Cadillac Escalade, offering serene comfort, premium materials, and the spaciousness of a true three-row luxury vehicle.

toyota/tundra.name: Tundra
toyota/tundra.description: The Toyota Tundra is a full-size pickup truck that brings Toyota reliability to the segment dominated by Detroit trucks. The third-generation Tundra features a twin-turbo V6 with available hybrid powertrain, replacing the previous V8. Known for exceptional durability and strong resale value.

toyota/4runner.name: 4Runner
toyota/4runner.description: The Toyota 4Runner is a body-on-frame midsize SUV built for off-road capability while serving as a practical daily driver. One of the last true truck-based SUVs in its class, the 4Runner has a dedicated following among outdoor enthusiasts. The sixth-generation 4Runner launched in 2025 with modern technology and a hybrid powertrain.

toyota/prius.name: Prius
toyota/prius.description: The Toyota Prius pioneered the hybrid vehicle segment and remains synonymous with fuel efficiency and eco-friendly driving. The fifth-generation Prius debuted with dramatically improved styling and performance while maintaining exceptional fuel economy. The Prius Prime plug-in hybrid offers extended electric-only range for daily commuting.

honda/pilot.name: Pilot
honda/pilot.description: The Honda Pilot is a three-row midsize SUV that combines family-friendly practicality with Honda engineering and reliability. Redesigned for the fourth generation, the Pilot offers a refined cabin, available TrailSport trim for light off-roading, and seating for up to eight passengers.

honda/odyssey.name: Odyssey
honda/odyssey.description: The Honda Odyssey is consistently rated among the best minivans available, offering versatile seating, a smooth ride, and Honda dependability. The Magic Slide second-row seats provide unmatched flexibility, and the available rear entertainment system keeps passengers entertained on long trips.

honda/hr-v.name: HR-V
honda/hr-v.description: The Honda HR-V is a subcompact crossover SUV that offers surprising interior space thanks to Honda Magic Seat flexibility. The second-generation HR-V grew in size and refinement, competing with the Toyota Corolla Cross and Hyundai Kona in the rapidly growing small SUV segment.

honda/ridgeline.name: Ridgeline
honda/ridgeline.description: The Honda Ridgeline is a unibody midsize pickup truck that prioritizes on-road comfort and daily drivability over traditional truck ruggedness. Unique features include an in-bed trunk, dual-action tailgate, and standard all-wheel drive. The Ridgeline appeals to buyers who want truck utility with car-like refinement.

ford/escape.name: Escape
ford/escape.description: The Ford Escape is a compact crossover SUV that has been a consistent top seller since its introduction. Available with gas, hybrid, and plug-in hybrid powertrains, the Escape offers versatile efficiency options for every buyer. The latest generation features sleek styling and Ford Co-Pilot360 driver assistance technology.

ford/bronco.name: Bronco
ford/bronco.description: The Ford Bronco returned in 2021 after a 25-year hiatus, offering serious off-road capability to rival the Jeep Wrangler. Available in two-door and four-door configurations with removable roof panels and doors, the Bronco combines rugged capability with modern technology.

ford/ranger.name: Ranger
ford/ranger.description: The Ford Ranger is a midsize pickup truck that offers a balance of capability and maneuverability for buyers who do not need a full-size truck. The current-generation Ranger features a turbocharged engine, available Tremor off-road package, and modern technology including a large touchscreen display.

ford/expedition.name: Expedition
ford/expedition.description: The Ford Expedition is a full-size three-row SUV built on a truck platform for maximum towing and passenger capacity. Available in standard and extended MAX wheelbases, the Expedition offers seating for up to eight with best-in-class cargo space.

ford/edge.name: Edge
ford/edge.description: The Ford Edge was a midsize two-row crossover SUV that offered a spacious interior and comfortable ride without the complexity of a third row. The Edge ST delivered performance-oriented driving dynamics with a twin-turbo V6. Ford discontinued the Edge after the 2024 model year.

chevrolet/tahoe.name: Tahoe
chevrolet/tahoe.description: The Chevrolet Tahoe is a full-size SUV that serves as the workhorse of American family hauling and towing. Built on a truck platform, the Tahoe offers seating for up to nine passengers, powerful V8 engines, and the ability to tow up to 8,400 pounds. The latest generation features an independent rear suspension for improved ride quality.

chevrolet/malibu.name: Malibu
chevrolet/malibu.description: The Chevrolet Malibu was a midsize sedan that offered affordable transportation with competitive fuel economy and a comfortable ride. The Malibu served as a value-oriented alternative to the Toyota Camry and Honda Accord for decades. Chevrolet discontinued the Malibu after the 2024 model year to focus on electric vehicles and SUVs.

chevrolet/traverse.name: Traverse
chevrolet/traverse.description: The Chevrolet Traverse is a three-row midsize crossover SUV that offers one of the most spacious interiors in its class. With seating for up to eight passengers and generous cargo capacity, the Traverse is designed for families who need maximum utility.

chevrolet/colorado.name: Colorado
chevrolet/colorado.description: The Chevrolet Colorado is a midsize pickup truck that offers truck capability in a more manageable size than the full-size Silverado. The ZR2 trim provides serious off-road performance with Multimatic DSSV dampers and locking differentials. The Colorado competes with the Toyota Tacoma and Ford Ranger.

chevrolet/camaro.name: Camaro
chevrolet/camaro.description: The Chevrolet Camaro is an iconic American muscle car that competed with the Ford Mustang and Dodge Challenger. Available as a coupe or convertible with engines ranging from a turbo-four to the supercharged ZL1 V8, the Camaro offered something for every performance enthusiast. Chevrolet ended Camaro production in 2024.

chevrolet/corvette.name: Corvette
chevrolet/corvette.description: The Chevrolet Corvette is America's sports car, delivering exotic-level performance at a fraction of the price of European rivals. The eighth-generation C8 Corvette moved to a mid-engine layout for the first time in the model's history. The Z06 and E-Ray hybrid variants push performance even further.

subaru/forester.name: Forester
subaru/forester.description: The Subaru Forester is a compact crossover SUV with standard all-wheel drive, excellent visibility, and a reputation for reliability and safety. The Forester consistently earns top safety ratings and is popular in regions with challenging weather conditions. The Wilderness trim adds enhanced off-road capability.

subaru/crosstrek.name: Crosstrek
subaru/crosstrek.description: The Subaru Crosstrek is a subcompact crossover that combines car-like fuel economy with SUV ground clearance and standard all-wheel drive. One of the most popular vehicles in the Subaru lineup, the Crosstrek appeals to active lifestyle buyers. A plug-in hybrid variant offers extended electric driving range.

subaru/impreza.name: Impreza
subaru/impreza.description: The Subaru Impreza is a compact car with standard symmetrical all-wheel drive, making it one of the most capable vehicles in its class for all-weather driving. Available as a hatchback, the Impreza offers practical transportation with Subaru safety technology and all-wheel-drive confidence.

subaru/wrx.name: WRX
subaru/wrx.description: The Subaru WRX is a performance sedan with a turbocharged boxer engine and standard all-wheel drive, born from Subaru's World Rally Championship heritage. The WRX offers accessible performance with everyday practicality, making it a favorite among enthusiasts.

subaru/legacy.name: Legacy
subaru/legacy.description: The Subaru Legacy is a midsize sedan with standard all-wheel drive, distinguishing it from virtually every competitor in its class. The Legacy offers a comfortable, refined driving experience with the confidence of all-weather traction. An available turbocharged engine adds performance to the capable platform.

subaru/ascent.name: Ascent
subaru/ascent.description: The Subaru Ascent is a three-row midsize SUV designed specifically for the North American market, offering seating for up to eight passengers. Standard all-wheel drive and a turbocharged boxer engine provide confident performance in all conditions. The Ascent was Subaru's first three-row vehicle.

subaru/brz.name: BRZ
subaru/brz.description: The Subaru BRZ is a lightweight rear-wheel-drive sports coupe developed jointly with Toyota. Known for its exceptional handling balance and accessible performance, the BRZ is a pure driver's car in an era of heavy, tech-laden vehicles. The second generation added more power while maintaining the lightweight formula.

acura/tlx.name: TLX
acura/tlx.description: The Acura TLX is a sport luxury sedan that combines precision handling with advanced technology and a premium interior. The Type S variant delivers genuine performance with a turbocharged V6 and torque-vectoring all-wheel drive. The TLX competes with the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes-Benz C-Class.

acura/mdx.name: MDX
acura/mdx.description: The Acura MDX is a three-row luxury SUV that has been one of the best-selling vehicles in its segment since its introduction. Known for combining Honda reliability with premium appointments and available Super Handling All-Wheel Drive. The MDX Type S adds a turbocharged V6 for enhanced performance.

acura/rdx.name: RDX
acura/rdx.description: The Acura RDX is a compact luxury crossover SUV that offers a turbocharged engine, a spacious interior, and Acura's precision-crafted design philosophy. The RDX features the True Touchpad Interface and available A-Spec styling for a sportier appearance. It competes with the Lexus NX and BMW X3.

acura/integra.name: Integra
acura/integra.description: The Acura Integra was revived in 2023 as a premium sport compact liftback, carrying on the legacy of the beloved original. Sharing its platform with the Honda Civic, the Integra offers a six-speed manual transmission and engaging driving dynamics. The Integra Type S delivers track-ready performance with a turbocharged engine.

dodge/charger.name: Charger
dodge/charger.description: The Dodge Charger is an American muscle sedan that combines aggressive styling with powerful engine options, including the legendary HEMI V8. The Charger SRT Hellcat and Redeye variants delivered supercharged performance exceeding 700 horsepower. Dodge has transitioned the Charger to an electrified platform for the next generation.

dodge/challenger.name: Challenger
dodge/challenger.description: The Dodge Challenger is a retro-styled muscle car that carried the torch for American V8 performance. From the V6 SXT to the supercharged Hellcat and the record-breaking Demon 170, the Challenger offered something for every performance enthusiast. Production ended in 2024 as Dodge transitions to electrified performance.

dodge/durango.name: Durango
dodge/durango.description: The Dodge Durango is a three-row performance SUV that stands apart from competitors with available V8 power and muscular styling. The Durango SRT and SRT Hellcat variants made it the fastest and most powerful three-row SUV available. The Durango combines family hauling capability with genuine performance credentials.

dodge/hornet.name: Hornet
dodge/hornet.description: The Dodge Hornet is a compact performance crossover that brings the brand's muscle car attitude to the growing small SUV segment. Available with a turbocharged engine or a plug-in hybrid R/T powertrain with over 280 horsepower. The Hornet marks Dodge's entry into the electrified performance crossover market.

gmc/sierra.name: Sierra
gmc/sierra.description: The GMC Sierra is a full-size pickup truck that shares its platform with the Chevrolet Silverado but adds premium features and distinctive styling. The Sierra Denali is one of the most luxurious trucks available, while the AT4 trim offers enhanced off-road capability. The Sierra was the first truck to offer a MultiPro tailgate with six unique functions.

gmc/yukon.name: Yukon
gmc/yukon.description: The GMC Yukon is a full-size SUV built on the same platform as the Chevrolet Tahoe, offering a premium experience with three rows of seating and powerful V8 engines. The Yukon Denali is the flagship model with exclusive features, while the Yukon XL provides additional cargo and passenger space. The current generation features an independent rear suspension for improved ride quality.

gmc/terrain.name: Terrain
gmc/terrain.description: The GMC Terrain is a compact crossover SUV that offers a refined cabin, good fuel economy, and GMC's professional-grade image. The Terrain competes with the Chevrolet Equinox and offers available all-wheel drive with a choice of turbocharged engines. The Denali trim adds premium materials and exclusive styling elements.

gmc/acadia.name: Acadia
gmc/acadia.description: The GMC Acadia is a midsize crossover SUV offering available three-row seating in a more manageable footprint than the full-size Yukon. The Acadia Denali and AT4 trims cater to luxury and adventure buyers respectively. The Acadia provides a good balance of passenger space, cargo capacity, and driving dynamics.

gmc/canyon.name: Canyon
gmc/canyon.description: The GMC Canyon is a midsize pickup truck that shares its platform with the Chevrolet Colorado but adds a more upscale presentation. The Canyon AT4X is one of the most capable off-road midsize trucks available, with Multimatic DSSV dampers and front and rear locking differentials. The Denali trim brings full-size luxury to the midsize segment.

genesis/gv70.name: GV70
genesis/gv70.description: The Genesis GV70 is a compact luxury SUV that quickly established itself as a serious competitor to the BMW X3 and Mercedes-Benz GLC. Offering a choice of turbocharged four-cylinder and twin-turbo V6 engines with available all-wheel drive. The GV70 delivers exceptional value with standard features that are optional on German rivals.

genesis/gv80.name: GV80
genesis/gv80.description: The Genesis GV80 is a midsize luxury SUV that announced Genesis as a legitimate luxury brand when it debuted. Available with three rows of seating, the GV80 features a serene cabin with premium materials and advanced technology. The GV80 competes with the BMW X5 and Mercedes-Benz GLE at a more accessible price point.

genesis/g70.name: G70
genesis/g70.description: The Genesis G70 is a compact sport sedan that has won multiple comparison tests against the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes-Benz C-Class. With a turbocharged 2.0T or powerful 3.3T twin-turbo V6, the G70 delivers engaging driving dynamics. Genesis includes complimentary scheduled maintenance and concierge service with every G70.

genesis/g80.name: G80
genesis/g80.description: The Genesis G80 is a midsize luxury sedan that competes with the BMW 5 Series and Mercedes-Benz E-Class. The G80 offers elegant design, a quiet and refined cabin, and an extensive list of standard features. An all-electric Electrified G80 variant brings EV luxury to the lineup.

mitsubishi/outlander.name: Outlander
mitsubishi/outlander.description: The Mitsubishi Outlander is a compact crossover SUV that offers available three-row seating and one of the most affordable plug-in hybrid options in the market. The Outlander PHEV provides substantial electric-only range for daily commuting while maintaining SUV versatility. The latest generation features a bold new design and partnership-derived technology from the Nissan-Mitsubishi alliance.

mitsubishi/eclipse-cross.name: Eclipse Cross
mitsubishi/eclipse-cross.description: The Mitsubishi Eclipse Cross is a compact crossover SUV that slots between the smaller Outlander Sport and the larger Outlander in the lineup. Featuring a distinctive coupe-like roofline and available Super All-Wheel Control, the Eclipse Cross offers a unique design in the crowded compact SUV market. Competitive pricing and a generous warranty make it a solid value proposition.

chrysler/pacifica.name: Pacifica
chrysler/pacifica.description: The Chrysler Pacifica is widely regarded as the best minivan on the market, offering a refined interior, innovative Stow 'n Go seating, and available plug-in hybrid powertrain. The Pacifica Hybrid was the first electrified minivan, providing significant fuel savings for family transportation. Available all-wheel drive and the Uconnect 5 infotainment system keep the Pacifica competitive.

chrysler/300.description: The Chrysler 300 was a full-size sedan that combined bold American styling with available V8 power and a rear-wheel-drive platform. The 300S offered a sportier driving experience, while the top-tier 300C featured the legendary 6.4-liter HEMI V8. Chrysler discontinued the 300 after the 2024 model year as the brand transitions toward electrification.

buick/enclave.name: Enclave
buick/enclave.description: The Buick Enclave is a three-row luxury crossover SUV that offers a quiet, comfortable cabin with premium features at a more accessible price than many luxury competitors. The Enclave's spacious interior seats up to seven or eight passengers, making it a popular family vehicle. Buick's QuietTuning technology ensures a serene driving experience.

buick/encore-gx.name: Encore GX
buick/encore-gx.description: The Buick Encore GX is a subcompact luxury crossover SUV that bridges the gap between the smaller Encore and the larger Envision. Offering available all-wheel drive and a choice of turbocharged three-cylinder engines, the Encore GX provides premium features in a compact package. The Sport Touring trim adds sporty visual elements and enhanced technology.

buick/envision.name: Envision
buick/envision.description: The Buick Envision is a compact luxury crossover SUV that offers a comfortable ride, a quiet cabin, and Buick's signature premium experience. Standard features include a turbocharged engine, an 8-inch touchscreen, and active safety technology. The Envision Avenir trim adds exclusive materials and design elements for a true luxury experience.

infiniti/q50.name: Q50
infiniti/q50.description: The Infiniti Q50 is a compact luxury sport sedan powered by a twin-turbocharged V6 engine, offering a balance of performance and everyday comfort. Available with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the Q50 Red Sport 400 delivers 400 horsepower for genuine sport sedan thrills.

infiniti/qx60.name: QX60
infiniti/qx60.description: The Infiniti QX60 is a three-row luxury crossover SUV that combines a refined cabin with family-friendly versatility. Completely redesigned with bold new styling and a luxurious interior, the QX60 competes with the Acura MDX and Lexus RX L.

infiniti/qx80.name: QX80
infiniti/qx80.description: The Infiniti QX80 is a full-size luxury SUV with seating for up to eight passengers and a powerful V8 engine. Known for its spacious cabin and commanding road presence, the QX80 competes with the Cadillac Escalade and Lincoln Navigator.

infiniti/qx50.name: QX50
infiniti/qx50.description: The Infiniti QX50 is a compact luxury crossover featuring the world's first production variable-compression turbo engine. The QX50 offers a spacious interior with premium materials and competes with the BMW X3 and Audi Q5.

mini/cooper.name: Cooper
mini/cooper.description: The Mini Cooper is an iconic compact car known for its go-kart-like handling, retro-modern design, and fun-to-drive character. Available in hardtop, convertible, and high-performance John Cooper Works variants, the Mini Cooper delivers driving excitement in a city-friendly package.

mini/countryman.name: Countryman
mini/countryman.description: The Mini Countryman is the brand's largest model, offering more passenger and cargo space while maintaining Mini's signature driving dynamics. Available with all-wheel drive and a plug-in hybrid powertrain, the Countryman brings versatility to the Mini lineup.

jaguar/f-pace.name: F-Pace
jaguar/f-pace.description: The Jaguar F-Pace is a luxury performance SUV that combines Jaguar's sporting heritage with everyday practicality. Offering a range of powertrains including a supercharged V8 in the SVR variant, the F-Pace delivers engaging driving dynamics unusual for its class.

jaguar/f-type.name: F-Type
jaguar/f-type.description: The Jaguar F-Type is a luxury sports car that carries on the legacy of the legendary E-Type. Available as a coupe or convertible with supercharged engines ranging from four cylinders to a thunderous V8, the F-Type is one of the most beautiful sports cars of its generation.

jaguar/e-pace.name: E-Pace
jaguar/e-pace.description: The Jaguar E-Pace is a compact luxury crossover SUV that brings Jaguar's design language and sporting character to the growing small luxury SUV segment. Standard all-wheel drive and a turbocharged engine provide confident performance in all conditions.

alfa-romeo/giulia.name: Giulia
alfa-romeo/giulia.description: The Alfa Romeo Giulia is an Italian sport sedan that prioritizes driving engagement above all else. The Quadrifoglio variant delivers 505 horsepower from a Ferrari-derived twin-turbo V6, making it one of the fastest sport sedans available. Stunning design and a driver-focused cockpit set the Giulia apart from German rivals.

alfa-romeo/stelvio.name: Stelvio
alfa-romeo/stelvio.description: The Alfa Romeo Stelvio is a compact luxury SUV that brings Italian passion and driving dynamics to the SUV segment. Named after the famous Stelvio Pass in the Italian Alps, the Stelvio Quadrifoglio variant is one of the fastest SUVs around the Nurburgring.

alfa-romeo/tonale.name: Tonale
alfa-romeo/tonale.description: The Alfa Romeo Tonale is a subcompact luxury crossover that expands the brand's SUV lineup with a more accessible entry point. Available with a plug-in hybrid powertrain, the Tonale features distinctive Italian styling and connects owners to the vehicle through an NFT-based digital certificate.

maserati/ghibli.name: Ghibli
maserati/ghibli.description: The Maserati Ghibli is an Italian luxury sport sedan named after a hot Saharan wind. Powered by Ferrari-built twin-turbo V6 engines, the Ghibli offers distinctive Italian design and an intoxicating exhaust note that set it apart from German competitors.

maserati/levante.name: Levante
maserati/levante.description: The Maserati Levante is an Italian luxury SUV that brings Maserati's grand touring character to the SUV segment. Available with twin-turbo V6 and V8 engines, the Levante combines genuine off-road capability with the soul of a sports car.

maserati/grecale.name: Grecale
maserati/grecale.description: The Maserati Grecale is a compact luxury SUV that competes with the Porsche Macan. Named after the Mediterranean wind, the Grecale offers multiple powertrain options including the electrified Folgore variant, representing Maserati's push toward electrification.

fiat/500x.name: 500X
fiat/500x.description: The Fiat 500X is a subcompact crossover SUV that combines Italian style with everyday practicality. Sharing its platform with the Jeep Renegade, the 500X offers available all-wheel drive and a turbocharged engine in a distinctive package.

fiat/500e.name: 500e
fiat/500e.description: The Fiat 500e is an all-electric city car that brings the iconic Cinquecento into the electric age. With retro-modern styling and zero emissions, the 500e is designed for urban driving with a range suitable for daily commuting.

polestar/polestar-2.name: Polestar 2
polestar/polestar-2.description: The Polestar 2 is a premium all-electric fastback sedan that competes directly with the Tesla Model 3. Built on Volvo's CMA platform, the Polestar 2 offers Scandinavian minimalist design, Google built-in infotainment, and available dual-motor all-wheel drive.

polestar/polestar-3.name: Polestar 3
polestar/polestar-3.description: The Polestar 3 is a luxury electric performance SUV designed to compete with the BMW iX and Mercedes EQE SUV. Built on Volvo's SPA2 platform with advanced aerodynamics, the Polestar 3 features a dual-motor powertrain and advanced lidar-based safety systems.

rivian/r1t.name: R1T
rivian/r1t.description: The Rivian R1T was the first electric pickup truck to reach production, offering a quad-motor drivetrain with up to 835 horsepower. With an integrated gear tunnel, powered tonneau cover, and adventure-oriented design, the R1T is purpose-built for outdoor lifestyles.

rivian/r1s.name: R1S
rivian/r1s.description: The Rivian R1S is a three-row electric SUV that shares its platform with the R1T pickup. Offering impressive off-road capability with up to 835 horsepower and over 300 miles of range, the R1S competes with the Land Rover Defender and Tesla Model X.

lucid/air.name: Air
lucid/air.description: The Lucid Air is an ultra-luxury electric sedan that holds the record for the longest-range EV with an EPA-estimated 516 miles. Designed by the former chief engineer of the Tesla Model S, the Air offers a spacious interior with a glass canopy roof and up to 1,234 horsepower in the Sapphire variant.

lucid/gravity.name: Gravity
lucid/gravity.description: The Lucid Gravity is a luxury electric SUV that brings Lucid's advanced EV technology to the three-row SUV segment. With seating for up to seven passengers and Lucid's efficient drivetrain technology, the Gravity targets the luxury SUV market dominated by the BMW X7 and Mercedes GLS.

lotus/emira.name: Emira
lotus/emira.description: The Lotus Emira is the brand's final internal combustion sports car, offering a choice of AMG-sourced four-cylinder turbo or Toyota-derived supercharged V6 engines. Following Colin Chapman's philosophy of lightweight engineering, the Emira delivers exceptional handling in a stunning mid-engine package.

lotus/eletre.name: Eletre
lotus/eletre.description: The Lotus Eletre is an all-electric hyper-SUV that marks Lotus's entry into the luxury electric SUV market. With up to 905 horsepower and a 0-60 time under 3 seconds, the Eletre combines Lotus's lightweight engineering expertise with cutting-edge EV technology.

bentley/continental-gt.name: Continental GT
bentley/continental-gt.description: The Bentley Continental GT is the definitive modern grand tourer, combining effortless power with handcrafted luxury. Powered by a twin-turbocharged W12 or V8 engine, the Continental GT can cross continents in supreme comfort while delivering genuine supercar performance.

bentley/bentayga.name: Bentayga
bentley/bentayga.description: The Bentley Bentayga was the first ultra-luxury SUV, setting a new benchmark for opulence in the SUV segment. Handcrafted at Bentley's Crewe factory with the finest leathers, woods, and metals, the Bentayga offers V8 power with plug-in hybrid efficiency available.

rolls-royce/cullinan.name: Cullinan
rolls-royce/cullinan.description: The Rolls-Royce Cullinan is the most luxurious SUV in the world, named after the largest diamond ever discovered. Powered by a twin-turbo V12 and featuring the signature coach doors, the Cullinan brings Rolls-Royce's magic carpet ride to all terrains.

rolls-royce/ghost.name: Ghost
rolls-royce/ghost.description: The Rolls-Royce Ghost is designed for owner-drivers who want the Rolls-Royce experience in a more dynamic package. The second-generation Ghost features a minimalist design philosophy with over 100kg of sound-deadening material for an eerily silent cabin.

rolls-royce/spectre.name: Spectre
rolls-royce/spectre.description: The Rolls-Royce Spectre is the brand's first fully electric vehicle, a luxury coupe that delivers the silent power befitting the world's most prestigious automaker. With 577 horsepower from dual electric motors and a range of over 260 miles, the Spectre represents the future of ultra-luxury motoring.

lamborghini/urus.name: Urus
lamborghini/urus.description: The Lamborghini Urus is a super SUV that combines Lamborghini's dramatic design and performance with everyday usability. Powered by a twin-turbo V8 producing 641 horsepower, the Urus is the fastest production SUV and has become Lamborghini's best-selling model.

lamborghini/huracan.name: Huracan
lamborghini/huracan.description: The Lamborghini Huracan is a mid-engine supercar powered by a naturally aspirated 5.2-liter V10 engine. Available in Coupe and Spyder body styles with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the Huracan delivers visceral performance with one of the greatest-sounding engines in automotive history.

lamborghini/revuelto.name: Revuelto
lamborghini/revuelto.description: The Lamborghini Revuelto is the successor to the Aventador, combining a naturally aspirated V12 with three electric motors for a combined 1,001 horsepower. The first Lamborghini plug-in hybrid, the Revuelto represents the brand's electrified future while preserving the emotional V12 experience.

ferrari/roma.name: Roma
ferrari/roma.description: The Ferrari Roma is a front-engine grand tourer that embodies the dolce vita spirit of 1960s Rome. With 612 horsepower from a twin-turbo V8, elegant proportions, and a refined cabin, the Roma is Ferrari's most accessible and versatile model.

ferrari/296-gtb.name: 296 GTB
ferrari/296-gtb.description: The Ferrari 296 GTB is a mid-engine plug-in hybrid supercar that pairs a twin-turbo V6 with an electric motor for 819 combined horsepower. The 296 GTB represents Ferrari's new era of electrified performance while introducing a completely new engine architecture.

ferrari/purosangue.name: Purosangue
ferrari/purosangue.description: The Ferrari Purosangue is the brand's first four-door, four-seat vehicle, powered by a naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12 producing 715 horsepower. Ferrari insists the Purosangue is not an SUV but a new segment of vehicle, combining Ferrari performance with four-door practicality for the first time.

mclaren/750s.name: 750S
mclaren/750s.description: The McLaren 750S is a supercar that replaces the 720S, offering 740 horsepower from a twin-turbo V8 in a carbon-fiber structure weighing just over 3,000 pounds. The 750S delivers race-car levels of performance while remaining usable as a grand tourer.

mclaren/artura.name: Artura
mclaren/artura.description: The McLaren Artura is the brand's first series-production hybrid supercar, combining a twin-turbo V6 with an electric motor for 671 combined horsepower. Built on an all-new carbon-fiber architecture, the Artura represents McLaren's transition toward electrified performance.

aston-martin/dbx.name: DBX
aston-martin/dbx.description: The Aston Martin DBX is the brand's first SUV, combining British luxury and craftsmanship with genuine performance capability. The DBX707 variant produces 697 horsepower, making it one of the most powerful luxury SUVs in the world.

aston-martin/db12.name: DB12
aston-martin/db12.description: The Aston Martin DB12 is billed as the world's first super tourer, replacing the iconic DB11 with 671 horsepower from a twin-turbo V8. The DB12 combines Aston Martin's timeless design with cutting-edge technology and devastating performance.

aston-martin/vantage.name: Vantage
aston-martin/vantage.description: The Aston Martin Vantage is the brand's pure sports car, designed to compete with the Porsche 911 and Mercedes-AMG GT. Powered by a twin-turbo V8, the Vantage delivers sharp handling and dramatic styling in a more compact package than the DB12.

bugatti/chiron.name: Chiron
bugatti/chiron.description: The Bugatti Chiron is one of the most extreme production cars ever made, powered by an 8.0-liter quad-turbocharged W16 engine producing 1,500 horsepower. Limited to 500 units worldwide, the Chiron can exceed 300 mph and represents the absolute pinnacle of automotive engineering.

bugatti/tourbillon.name: Tourbillon
bugatti/tourbillon.description: The Bugatti Tourbillon is the successor to the Chiron, combining a naturally aspirated V16 engine with three electric motors for approximately 1,800 horsepower. Named after the precision watchmaking mechanism, the Tourbillon represents Bugatti's vision for the future of hyper-luxury performance.

maybach/s-class-maybach.name: S-Class Maybach
maybach/s-class-maybach.description: The Mercedes-Maybach S-Class is the pinnacle of luxury sedan motoring, featuring an extended wheelbase, reclining rear seats, and the finest materials available. Powered by a twin-turbo V8 or V12 engine, the Maybach S-Class competes with Rolls-Royce and Bentley.

maybach/gls-maybach.name: GLS Maybach
maybach/gls-maybach.description: The Mercedes-Maybach GLS is an ultra-luxury SUV that transforms the GLS platform into a four-seat limousine on stilts. With executive rear seating, a refrigerated champagne compartment, and a twin-turbo V8, the Maybach GLS competes with the Bentley Bentayga and Rolls-Royce Cullinan.

saab/9-3.description: The Saab 9-3 was a compact executive car that embodied Saab's aviation-inspired engineering with turbocharged performance and distinctive Scandinavian design. Known for its unique ignition placement between the front seats and strong safety credentials, the 9-3 developed a loyal following among enthusiasts who valued its blend of quirkiness and capability.

saab/9-5.description: The Saab 9-5 was a midsize luxury sedan that served as the brand's flagship, offering turbocharged power, a spacious cabin, and Saab's commitment to safety innovation. The second-generation 9-5 launched in 2010 with striking design but saw limited production before Saab's bankruptcy in 2011.

saab/9-2x.name: 9-2X
saab/9-2x.description: The Saab 9-2X was a compact wagon based on the Subaru Impreza, offering standard all-wheel drive and a turbocharged engine option in the Aero trim. Affectionately nicknamed the 'Saabaru' by enthusiasts, the 9-2X was a unique blend of Subaru capability and Saab styling that lasted only two model years.

saab/9-7x.name: 9-7X
saab/9-7x.description: The Saab 9-7X was a midsize SUV based on the Chevrolet TrailBlazer platform, representing Saab's entry into the American SUV market. It featured Saab-specific styling cues and an available V8 engine, offering a more refined experience than its GM platform-mate despite its truck-based underpinnings.

saab/900.description: The Saab 900 was the quintessential Saab, renowned for its turbocharged engines, distinctive wraparound windshield, and aircraft-inspired dashboard. The 900 Convertible became a cultural icon and is considered one of the most desirable Saabs ever produced, helping establish the brand's identity in North America.

saturn/aura.name: Aura
saturn/aura.description: The Saturn Aura was a midsize sedan that earned the 2007 North American Car of the Year award, signaling Saturn's move toward competitive mainstream vehicles. Built on GM's Epsilon platform shared with the Pontiac G6, the Aura offered a refined ride, available V6 power, and a hybrid variant.

saturn/vue.name: Vue
saturn/vue.description: The Saturn Vue was a compact crossover SUV that pioneered Saturn's move into the growing SUV segment. The second-generation Vue offered a Green Line hybrid variant and was one of the first affordable hybrid SUVs available to American consumers.

saturn/outlook.name: Outlook
saturn/outlook.description: The Saturn Outlook was a full-size three-row crossover SUV that shared its Lambda platform with the GMC Acadia and Buick Enclave. The Outlook offered seating for up to eight passengers with a spacious interior and car-like driving dynamics uncommon in vehicles of its size.

saturn/ion.name: Ion
saturn/ion.description: The Saturn Ion was a compact car that replaced the iconic S-Series, featuring Saturn's signature dent-resistant polymer body panels. The Ion Red Line variant offered a supercharged Ecotec engine and sport-tuned suspension, giving the compact Saturn legitimate performance credentials.

saturn/sky.name: Sky
saturn/sky.description: The Saturn Sky was a two-seat roadster that shared its Kappa platform with the Pontiac Solstice, offering open-air driving excitement at an accessible price. The Sky Red Line featured a turbocharged engine producing 260 horsepower, making it one of the most exciting vehicles Saturn ever produced.

saturn/sl.name: SL
saturn/sl.description: The Saturn SL was the original Saturn sedan that helped define the brand with its dent-resistant polymer body panels and no-haggle pricing philosophy. The SL offered practical, fuel-efficient transportation and cultivated a devoted owner community that celebrated the brand at annual Homecoming events in Spring Hill, Tennessee.

pontiac/g6.name: G6
pontiac/g6.description: The Pontiac G6 was a midsize car that gained massive publicity when Oprah Winfrey gave away 276 of them to her studio audience in 2004. Available as a sedan, coupe, and retractable hardtop convertible, the G6 offered versatility and style as Pontiac's volume seller.

pontiac/grand-am.name: Grand Am
pontiac/grand-am.description: The Pontiac Grand Am was one of the best-selling compact cars in America during its production run, known for its aggressive styling and sport-tuned suspension. The Grand Am GT with its RAM Air hood and distinctive body cladding was a common sight on American roads throughout the early 2000s.

pontiac/grand-prix.name: Grand Prix
pontiac/grand-prix.description: The Pontiac Grand Prix was a midsize sedan with strong NASCAR heritage, known for its powerful supercharged V6 engine in the GTP trim. The Grand Prix GXP with its V8 engine represented the pinnacle of front-wheel-drive performance sedans from General Motors.

pontiac/gto.name: GTO
pontiac/gto.description: The Pontiac GTO was a rebadged Holden Monaro from Australia, reviving one of the most legendary muscle car nameplates in American history. Powered by a Corvette-derived LS-series V8 with up to 400 horsepower, the GTO offered tremendous performance value but had modest sales due to its understated styling.

pontiac/firebird.name: Firebird
pontiac/firebird.description: The Pontiac Firebird and its iconic Trans Am variant were among America's most celebrated sports cars, offering V8 power and aggressive styling. The WS6 performance package with the Ram Air V8 made the fourth-generation Firebird one of the best performance bargains of its era.

pontiac/solstice.name: Solstice
pontiac/solstice.description: The Pontiac Solstice was a two-seat roadster that proved Pontiac could still build exciting cars in the brand's final years. The Solstice GXP featured a turbocharged engine producing 260 horsepower, and the rare Solstice Coupe is now highly sought after by collectors.

pontiac/vibe.name: Vibe
pontiac/vibe.description: The Pontiac Vibe was a compact hatchback developed jointly with Toyota, sharing its platform and powertrain with the Toyota Matrix. This collaboration gave the Vibe Toyota's renowned reliability, and the Vibe GT offered a high-revving 180-horsepower engine from the Corolla XRS.

oldsmobile/cutlass.name: Cutlass
oldsmobile/cutlass.description: The Oldsmobile Cutlass carried one of the most storied nameplates in American automotive history, as the original Cutlass was America's best-selling car throughout much of the 1970s. The final-generation Cutlass was a midsize sedan that served as a bridge between Oldsmobile's glorious past and its uncertain future.

oldsmobile/alero.name: Alero
oldsmobile/alero.description: The Oldsmobile Alero was a compact car that served as the brand's final attempt to attract younger buyers with sportier styling and available V6 power. The very last Oldsmobile ever produced was a 2004 Alero, ending over 100 years of continuous Oldsmobile production.

oldsmobile/intrigue.name: Intrigue
oldsmobile/intrigue.description: The Oldsmobile Intrigue was a midsize sedan powered by a responsive 3.5-liter V6 engine, earning praise for its balanced handling and refined ride quality. The Intrigue represented Oldsmobile's attempt to redefine itself as a driver-focused brand but could not reverse the marque's declining sales.

oldsmobile/bravada.name: Bravada
oldsmobile/bravada.description: The Oldsmobile Bravada was a midsize luxury SUV that offered standard all-wheel drive and a refined on-road experience compared to its truck-based competitors. The third-generation Bravada shared its platform with the Chevrolet TrailBlazer but added upscale features and a smoother ride befitting the Oldsmobile brand.

oldsmobile/aurora.name: Aurora
oldsmobile/aurora.description: The Oldsmobile Aurora was a full-size luxury sedan that represented Oldsmobile's most ambitious attempt to compete with imports like the Lexus ES and Acura TL. Powered by a smooth Northstar-derived V8 or later a Shortstar V6, the Aurora featured sleek styling that deliberately omitted Oldsmobile badging to attract new buyers.

mercury/grand-marquis.name: Grand Marquis
mercury/grand-marquis.description: The Mercury Grand Marquis was a full-size body-on-frame sedan that shared its Panther platform with the Ford Crown Victoria and Lincoln Town Car. Known for its smooth V8 power, spacious bench-seat cabin, and comfortable ride, the Grand Marquis was a favorite among traditional American car buyers and fleet operators.

mercury/sable.name: Sable
mercury/sable.description: The Mercury Sable was a midsize sedan that served as the upscale companion to the Ford Taurus, sharing its platform while offering more premium appointments. The Sable's oval-themed design in its later years was polarizing, but it remained a solid choice for buyers seeking a comfortable, well-equipped family sedan.

mercury/mountaineer.name: Mountaineer
mercury/mountaineer.description: The Mercury Mountaineer was a midsize SUV based on the Ford Explorer, offering a more luxurious take on the popular Explorer formula. The Mountaineer featured a standard V8 engine in early years and added premium interior materials and quieter ride quality to distinguish itself from its Ford sibling.

mercury/mariner.name: Mariner
mercury/mariner.description: The Mercury Mariner was a compact SUV based on the Ford Escape, offering a slightly more upscale appearance and additional standard features. The Mariner Hybrid was one of the first hybrid compact SUVs available, demonstrating Mercury's effort to modernize its lineup before the brand's discontinuation.

mercury/milan.name: Milan
mercury/milan.description: The Mercury Milan was a midsize sedan based on the Ford Fusion that offered a more refined alternative with premium features and styling. The Milan Hybrid matched the Fusion Hybrid's impressive fuel economy while adding Mercury's upscale touches, making it one of the brand's final success stories.
