massachusetts.safetyInspectionDetails: Massachusetts requires an annual safety inspection for every registered vehicle. The inspection is $35 for most vehicles. A vehicle operated only on electricity still needs the safety inspection.
massachusetts.registrationNotes: Registration is biennial. A 6.25 percent sales tax applies to a purchase.
massachusetts.description: Massachusetts requires an annual safety inspection. A vehicle that runs only on electricity does not take the emissions portion. The state has strong consumer protections and EV incentive programs.

michigan.name: Michigan
michigan.insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / PIP coverage required
michigan.lemonLawSummary: Michigan's lemon law, Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 257.1402 and 257.1403, asks the owner to report the defect during the express warranty or within one year of delivery, whichever is earlier, and it sets no mileage cap. The presumption is four repairs of the same defect within two years of the first repair attempt, or 30 days out of service during the warranty or that first year. After the third repair, send written notice by return receipt; the manufacturer then has five business days to repair. On the days-out path, written notice goes out after 25 days in the shop, and the manufacturer again has five business days.
michigan.registrationFeeRange: Based on the vehicle's list price
michigan.registrationNotes: The first registration of a passenger vehicle from model year 1984 or newer is set by list price under MCL 257.801. The tax is $36 when the list price is $6,000 or less. Above $6,000 the tax steps by $6 for each $1,000 of list price. Above $30,000 the tax is $178 plus $6 for each $1,000 or fraction over $30,000. The second registration is 90 percent of the first. The third is 90 percent of the second. Later registrations stay at 90 percent of the third. List price is the base list price published by the secretary of state, or the price on the window label when that list is not published. The Michigan Secretary of State fee chart follows this statute.
michigan.evRegistrationDetails: A vehicle that runs only on electricity and weighs 8,000 pounds or less has a statutory add-on of $100. The add-on rises with the gasoline tax above 19 cents a gallon under MCL 257.801.
michigan.description: Michigan is a no-fault insurance state with unique auto insurance requirements. As the heart of the American auto industry, the state has comprehensive vehicle laws and strong consumer protections.

minnesota.name: Minnesota
minnesota.insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $40,000 PIP
minnesota.lemonLawSummary: Minn. Stat. § 325F.665 places the presumption in the express warranty or in the two years after delivery, and the date that comes first ends it. Miles do not shorten that window. A problem first reported while the warranty was still running can still support a refund or replacement from attempts made within three years of delivery. The presumption is four repairs, 30 business days out of service, or a single repair of a complete brake or steering failure that is likely to cause death or serious injury, and the four-repair and 30-day routes need written notice plus a chance to cure.
minnesota.evIncentiveDetails: Minnesota's EV rebate funding is currently exhausted.
minnesota.emissionsDetails: Minnesota's Twin Cities auto emissions inspection program ended on March 1, 2000, when the Legislature repealed it. The state does not require an emissions test to register a vehicle.
minnesota.registrationNotes: The percentage applies to a vehicle first registered in Minnesota on or after November 16, 2020. The share of MSRP falls with age. From the 11th year the amount added to the base is $20.
minnesota.evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays a surcharge of $150, or a greater amount based on age and MSRP.
minnesota.description: Minnesota requires liability insurance and has a no-fault insurance component. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and offers growing incentives for EV adoption.

mississippi.name: Mississippi
mississippi.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
mississippi.lemonLawSummary: Miss. Code Ann. § 63-17-159 keeps the repair presumption inside the express warranty or the first year after delivery, whichever finishes sooner. The section does not add a mileage limit. Substantially the same problem repaired three times, or 15 working days in the shop for that problem, is enough, and routine maintenance is not part of the 15 days. Write the manufacturer before you rely on the section; once the car is at the shop the manufacturer names, that shop has ten working days to make it conform.
mississippi.registrationFeeRange: $12.75 to renew or $14 for a first registration
mississippi.registrationNotes: A passenger vehicle also pays a $15 privilege tax. Local ad valorem tax is charged as well.
mississippi.description: Mississippi requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles and has a lemon law for new vehicle purchases. The state does not require emissions testing or annual safety inspections.

missouri.name: Missouri
missouri.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
missouri.lemonLawSummary: Under Mo. Rev. Stat. §§ 407.565 and 407.571, the clock runs for the express warranty or for one year after delivery, and the period that ends first controls. There is no mileage cutoff in that test. The same problem repaired four times, or the car held for repair for 30 working days, meets the presumption, and days spent on ordinary maintenance stay out of the count. Tell the manufacturer or its agent about the problem before that window closes.
missouri.emissionsDetails: The Gateway Vehicle Inspection Program tests gasoline vehicles from model year 1996 and diesel vehicles from model year 1997, at or under 8,500 pounds, that are registered in St. Louis City or in St. Louis, St. Charles, or Jefferson County. Franklin County residents have been exempt since July 1, 2022. Kansas City is not in the program. The state cap on the emissions inspection fee is $24. Even model years are tested in even calendar years, and odd model years in odd calendar years. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
missouri.safetyInspectionDetails: RSMo § 307.350 requires a biennial safety inspection, in the even calendar year for an even model year and in the odd calendar year for an odd model year, and also when ownership changes. A vehicle is exempt for the first ten model years if it has fewer than 150,000 miles, other than a prior salvage vehicle right after it is rebuilt. The certificate is generally valid for 60 days. The Department of Revenue said on January 6, 2026, that these rules had not changed.
missouri.registrationNotes: A $9 processing fee is added to a one-year registration.
missouri.description: Missouri requires liability insurance. Safety inspections are biennial, with an exemption for many newer low-mileage vehicles. Emissions testing applies in the St. Louis area and not in Kansas City. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles.

montana.name: Montana
montana.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
montana.lemonLawSummary: Montana defines the warranty period in Mont. Code Ann. §§ 61-4-501 and 61-4-504 as two years or 18,000 miles, whichever is earlier. The presumption is four repairs of the same problem, or 30 business days out of service after the manufacturer, its agent, or a dealer was notified. Send written notice to the manufacturer or its agent while the warranty period is still open. The manufacturer has to tell the buyer that written notice is required, and the presumption is not used against a manufacturer that never received that notice and a chance to cure.
montana.registrationFeeRange: $217 at 0 to 4 years, $87 at 5 to 10 years, or $28 at 11 years or older
montana.registrationNotes: A county option tax is also charged.
montana.description: Montana is popular for vehicle registration due to its lack of sales tax. The state requires liability insurance but does not mandate emissions testing or safety inspections for most vehicles.

nebraska.name: Nebraska
nebraska.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
nebraska.lemonLawSummary: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-2704 times the presumption to the express warranty or to one year after delivery, and the earlier of those two dates ends it. The statute does not set a mileage limit. The car meets the test after four repairs of the same problem or after 40 days out of service. That test is available only once the manufacturer has notice by certified mail and a chance to cure.
nebraska.registrationNotes: The motor vehicle tax is based on MSRP and age.
nebraska.evRegistrationDetails: An electric or hydrogen passenger vehicle pays a $150 alternative-fuel fee. A plug-in electric passenger vehicle pays $75.
nebraska.description: Nebraska requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing and has a motor vehicle tax based on vehicle value.

nevada.name: Nevada
nevada.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
nevada.lemonLawSummary: Nevada asks the buyer to report the problem in writing under NRS 597.610 before the express warranty ends or one year after delivery to the original buyer, whichever is earlier. NRS 597.630 then presumes enough attempts after four repairs of the same problem or 30 calendar days out of service. The 30-day count can run longer when the needed repair is delayed for reasons outside the manufacturer's or dealer's control.
nevada.emissionsDetails: Qualifying gasoline vehicles based in urban Clark County or Washoe County need an annual test beginning with the fourth registration. The 2026 maximum for a light-duty gasoline test is $75.50 in Clark County and $71.50 in Washoe County. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
nevada.registrationNotes: Governmental services tax is based on the vehicle's value.
nevada.description: Nevada requires liability insurance and emissions testing in the Las Vegas and Reno metro areas. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and offers growing EV incentive programs.

new-hampshire.name: New Hampshire
new-hampshire.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage. Note: Insurance is not mandatory in New Hampshire, but these minimums apply if you carry coverage.
new-hampshire.lemonLawSummary: New Hampshire's presumption in RSA 357-D:3, VII is measured during the express warranty. Three repairs of the same problem, or 30 business days out of service, meets the presumption, counting a business day as a day those dealers normally keep a service department open. Repair attempts should be on written repair orders, generally at the same dealer, and a car the owner can use for a major part of the day is not out of service. After the third repair or after those 30 business days, RSA 357-D:4 requires written notice to the manufacturer, which then gets one final chance to repair.
new-hampshire.safetyInspectionDetails: The New Hampshire DMV's February 13, 2026 guidance says the vehicle inspection program is suspended until further notice. Stations are not issuing state inspection stickers, and an annual inspection is not required while that suspension stands. Drivers remain responsible for the equipment rules in RSA 266. OBD emissions testing was part of that inspection. The status can change.
new-hampshire.registrationFeeRange: $42 up to 3,000 lb, $48 from 3,001 to 5,000 lb, or $66 from 5,001 to 8,000 lb
new-hampshire.registrationNotes: The town or city also charges a permit fee. There is no sales tax on the purchase.
new-hampshire.description: New Hampshire does not require drivers to carry auto insurance, though they remain financially responsible for damages. The DMV's February 13, 2026 guidance suspends the vehicle inspection program until further notice.

new-jersey.name: New Jersey
new-jersey.insuranceMinimumDetail: $35,000 bodily injury per person / $70,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage / PIP $15,000 minimum, up to $250,000 for certain injuries. The basic policy is also legal: no bodily injury coverage or an optional $10,000, $5,000 property damage, and $15,000 PIP.
new-jersey.lemonLawSummary: New Jersey's lemon law, N.J.S.A. 56:12-33, uses the first 24,000 miles or two years, and a motorhome uses 45 calendar days out of service where a passenger car uses 20. Three repairs of substantially the same problem, that days-out total, or one exam of a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, is the presumption. It applies only after the manufacturer received certified-mail notice, return receipt requested, and had one chance to repair within 10 calendar days. That letter may go out after two repairs, after the car has been out 20 calendar days (45 for a motorhome), or after one exam of a serious safety problem.
new-jersey.evIncentiveDetails: Charge Up New Jersey offers $1,500 at the dealer for an eligible new EV, or $4,000 total for income-qualified Charge Up+ applicants, plus up to $250 toward a home Level 2 charger.
new-jersey.emissionsDetails: New Jersey requires biennial emissions inspections for most vehicles 5+ model years old. Testing is performed at state Motor Vehicle Commission inspection stations at no charge. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
new-jersey.registrationFeeRange: $46.50 or $59 under 3,500 lb, and $71.50 or $84 above 3,500 lb
new-jersey.registrationNotes: The lower amount in each pair is for a model older than two years. The higher amount is for a model within two years.
new-jersey.evRegistrationDetails: A zero-emission vehicle pays an added annual fee of $250 beginning July 1, 2024. That fee rises by $10 a year for four years.
new-jersey.description: New Jersey requires no-fault insurance with some of the highest minimum coverage requirements in the nation. The state mandates emissions testing and has strong consumer protection laws.

new-mexico.name: New Mexico
new-mexico.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
new-mexico.lemonLawSummary: NMSA 1978 § 57-16A-3(C) covers a new vehicle for the express warranty or for the year after delivery, and the presumption follows the date that arrives first. Miles are not a separate cutoff. Four repairs that leave the same problem uncorrected, or 30 business days the car sits with the manufacturer, an agent, or a dealer, meets the test, not counting routine maintenance. Direct written notice and a chance to cure have to come first, and the manufacturer must say so in the warranty or in a separate notice.
new-mexico.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing applies to vehicles registered or commuting in Bernalillo County. Vehicles from 1991 and newer, up to 10,000 pounds, are tested every two years and at a change of ownership. A brand-new vehicle is exempt for four years after the first registration on the manufacturer certificate of origin. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
new-mexico.registrationFeeRange: Based on shipping weight and years registered
new-mexico.registrationNotes: Chapter 4 of the 2026 laws set the twelve-month fees. After five years of registration the fees are $26.25, $38.75, and $56.25. Before that they are $33.75, $48.75, and $70. Each registration includes a $1.50 tire recycling fee.
new-mexico.evRegistrationDetails: An additional electric-vehicle fee of $70 starts on January 1, 2027.
new-mexico.description: New Mexico requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles. The state has emissions testing in the Albuquerque area and a lemon law covering new vehicle purchases.

new-york.name: New York
new-york.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $50,000 PIP (no-fault) required
new-york.lemonLawSummary: New York's general presumption in General Business Law § 198-a(d) covers the first 18,000 miles or two years. Four repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service, is the test for a car. During that period, report the problem to the manufacturer, its agent, or an authorized dealer, and the agent or dealer has seven days to forward written notice by certified mail. Motor homes in the same section follow a different path: certified-mail notice after two repairs or 21 days out of service, and the owner may proceed after three repairs or 30 days out, if the manufacturer gave prior written notice of that requirement.
new-york.evIncentiveDetails: NYSERDA's Drive Clean Rebate takes $500 to $2,000 off eligible new EVs at participating dealers, based on range and MSRP. Utilities such as Con Edison offer additional charging programs.
new-york.emissionsDetails: Annual emissions testing is required statewide as part of the annual safety inspection for most vehicles 2+ model years old. OBD-II testing is used for 1996+ model year vehicles. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
new-york.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, steering, tires, lights, glass, exhaust, and emissions. Cost varies by shop but is typically $10-$37.
new-york.registrationNotes: The weight schedule is the two-year fee. New York City residents also pay a supplemental registration fee. Sales tax varies by county.
new-york.description: New York has comprehensive vehicle ownership requirements including no-fault insurance, annual safety and emissions inspections, and one of the strongest lemon laws in the nation.

north-carolina.name: North Carolina
north-carolina.insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
north-carolina.lemonLawSummary: North Carolina allows a refund or replacement under N.C.G.S. § 20-351.3 for a defect that substantially impairs value and showed up no later than 24 months or 24,000 miles after delivery. The presumption in § 20-351.5 is four repairs of the same problem that still exists, or 20 business days out of service during any 12-month period of the warranty. Express warranties have to last at least one year or 12,000 miles, and the repair duty runs for one year or the express-warranty term, whichever is longer. Notify the manufacturer directly in writing and allow up to 15 calendar days to correct the problem, unless it never disclosed that written notice was required; § 20-351.7 also requires a separate 10-day written notice before you sue.
north-carolina.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is part of the annual inspection in 19 counties. Session Law 2023-134 and Session Law 2026-41 end that emissions program after EPA approval, and the annual safety inspection remains statewide. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
north-carolina.safetyInspectionDetails: North Carolina requires an annual safety inspection statewide for registered vehicles. The emissions portion, where it still applies, is limited to 19 counties and is separate from the statewide safety inspection.
north-carolina.evRegistrationDetails: A plug-in electric vehicle that uses no other power source pays an additional $214.50. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $107.25.
north-carolina.description: North Carolina requires liability insurance and an annual safety inspection statewide. Emissions testing remains in 19 counties until EPA approves the end of that program.

north-dakota.name: North Dakota
north-dakota.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
north-dakota.lemonLawSummary: N.D.C.C. § 51-07-19 measures repairs during the express warranty or during the year after delivery, and the shorter of those two periods is the one that counts. There is no mileage cap on that presumption. More than three repairs of the same problem, which means a fourth visit while the trouble is still present, or 30 business days out of service, is the presumption. It does not run against the manufacturer until the manufacturer has had direct notice and a chance to cure.
north-dakota.registrationNotes: The 2026 schedule uses weight and the year first registered, not the model year.
north-dakota.evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays an additional $120 road-use fee. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $50.
north-dakota.description: North Dakota requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections and has some of the lowest insurance rates in the nation.

ohio.name: Ohio
ohio.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
ohio.lemonLawSummary: Ohio's lemon law, Ohio Rev. Code § 1345.73, uses the first year or 18,000 miles, whichever is earlier, the same window § 1345.72 uses for reporting a repair. Three repairs of substantially the same problem, 30 calendar days out of service, eight attempts to repair any problems, or one attempt at a problem likely to cause death or serious bodily injury, is enough if the problem continues or comes back. Report the nonconformity to the manufacturer, its agent, or its authorized dealer during that year or 18,000 miles.
ohio.emissionsDetails: E-Check applies in Cuyahoga, Geauga, Lake, Lorain, Medina, Portage, and Summit counties. Gasoline and diesel vehicles that are 6 to 25 years old, and non-plug-in hybrids that are 7 to 25 years old, are tested every two years at 10,000 pounds or less. An established Ohio resident gets one free passing test in 365 days. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
ohio.registrationNotes: The deputy registrar fee for one year is $8. County permissive tax cannot exceed $30. A replacement plate is $15 for one plate or $16.25 for two. A hybrid pays an additional $100 a year.
ohio.evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays an additional $200 a year. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $150 a year.
ohio.description: Ohio requires liability insurance but is unique in that it uses a financial responsibility law rather than mandatory insurance. The state requires emissions testing in certain urban counties.

oklahoma.name: Oklahoma
oklahoma.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
oklahoma.lemonLawSummary: 15 O.S. § 901(D) places Oklahoma's presumption inside the express warranty or the year after delivery, and the period that ends first is the one that applies. Mileage is not part of that cutoff. The same problem repaired four times, or 30 business days in the shop, creates the presumption. Put the report in writing to the manufacturer during the warranty or that year; without that notice and a chance to cure, the presumption does not apply.
oklahoma.registrationFeeRange: Based on the year of registration
oklahoma.registrationNotes: The fee is $96 for registration years 1 through 4. It then steps down to $26 from year 17 on. The motor vehicle excise tax is 3.25 percent of vehicle value.
oklahoma.description: Oklahoma requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing but mandates personal property taxes on vehicles, known as excise tax.

oregon.name: Oregon
oregon.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
oregon.lemonLawSummary: Oregon's lemon law, ORS 646A.406, uses two years after delivery or 24,000 miles, whichever ends first. The presumption is three repairs plus a chance to cure, 30 calendar days out of service (60 for a motor home), or one repair plus a final attempt on a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, if the problem continues. Before the presumption is used, the manufacturer needs a direct letter about the defect and a chance to correct it.
oregon.evIncentiveDetails: Oregon's Clean Vehicle Rebate covers purchases and leases from August 25 to November 4, 2026 only, and funds are running low; late applications may be waitlisted until spring 2027. Oregon has no sales tax on vehicle purchases.
oregon.emissionsDetails: Non-exempt passenger vehicles in the Portland and Medford areas are tested every two years. The DEQ test fee is $25 in Portland and $20 in Medford, and only after a passing result. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
oregon.registrationFeeRange: $126 at 0 to 19 MPG, $136 at 20 to 39 MPG, or $216 at 40 MPG or higher
oregon.registrationNotes: A new passenger vehicle with a manufacturer certificate of origin is registered for four years, and that registration fee is doubled. Multnomah County adds $112. Washington County and Clackamas County add $60.
oregon.evRegistrationDetails: An all-electric passenger vehicle that is not enrolled in OReGO pays $376 for two years. The title fee for that vehicle is $192. The miles-per-gallon schedule does not apply.
oregon.description: Oregon has no sales tax on vehicle purchases and requires emissions testing in the Portland metro area. The state has a strong lemon law and offers significant incentives for electric vehicles.

pennsylvania.name: Pennsylvania
pennsylvania.insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $5,000 property damage
pennsylvania.lemonLawSummary: Pennsylvania's Automobile Lemon Law, the Act of March 28, 1984, P.L. 150, No. 28, covers a car for one year, 12,000 miles, or the warranty, whichever comes first. A motorcycle uses one year or the warranty, and the statute does not add a mileage cap for motorcycles. Three repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service, is the presumption in section 6. When the car comes back to the same dealer a second time for the same problem, section 7 says the dealer notifies the manufacturer by certified mail within seven days.
pennsylvania.lemonLawCitation: Automobile Lemon Law, Act of Mar. 28, 1984, P.L. 150, No. 28, § 6
pennsylvania.emissionsDetails: Annual emissions testing is required in 25 counties. The emissions sticker has no state fee. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
pennsylvania.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for every registered vehicle. The official inspection sticker fee is $12.
pennsylvania.registrationNotes: A 6 percent sales tax applies to a purchase.
pennsylvania.description: Pennsylvania requires liability insurance and annual safety and emissions inspections. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and is part of a multi-state emissions standards agreement.

rhode-island.name: Rhode Island
rhode-island.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
rhode-island.lemonLawSummary: Rhode Island's term of protection in R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.2-1 is one year or 15,000 miles, and the presumption is in § 31-5.2-5. Four repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service, during that term is the test, and the manufacturer also gets one more cure of not more than seven calendar days. Report the nonconformity during the term of protection. The extra seven days starts when the manufacturer first knows the four-repair or 30-day limit has been met.
rhode-island.lemonLawCitation: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.2-5; term of protection defined in § 31-5.2-1
rhode-island.emissionsDetails: Gas and diesel light-duty vehicles take the emissions test with the safety inspection every 24 months. A new vehicle is exempt for two years from purchase or until 24,000 miles, whichever comes first. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
rhode-island.safetyInspectionDetails: A light-duty vehicle of 8,500 pounds or less must pass a safety and emissions inspection at least once every 24 months. The fee for that inspection is $55.
rhode-island.registrationFeeRange: $30 a year up to 4,000 lb gross weight
rhode-island.registrationNotes: A two-year passenger renewal also adds a $3.50 technology surcharge for each year. It adds a $20 department of transportation surcharge for each year. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $100 per registration year. A non-plug-in hybrid pays an additional $50 per registration year.
rhode-island.evRegistrationDetails: A battery-electric vehicle pays an additional $200 per registration year.
rhode-island.description: Rhode Island requires liability insurance and biennial safety and emissions inspections. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and eliminated the car excise tax in recent years.

south-carolina.name: South Carolina
south-carolina.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
south-carolina.lemonLawSummary: South Carolina, in S.C. Code §§ 56-28-30 and 56-28-40, asks for a report within the first 12 months or 12,000 miles, while the presumption counts repairs and days during the express warranty. The presumption is met by three repairs aimed at the same problem, or by 30 calendar days the car spends out of service. If the manufacturer clearly said at the sale that written notice is required, send that notice so it can make a final repair. It then has ten business days to name a franchised shop and ten business days after delivery to attempt the repair.
south-carolina.lemonLawCitation: S.C. Code Ann. § 56-28-40; repair term in § 56-28-30
south-carolina.registrationNotes: The infrastructure maintenance fee is 5 percent of the purchase price and is capped at $500. Personal property tax is also assessed.
south-carolina.evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle is charged $120 plus the registration fee.
south-carolina.description: South Carolina requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or annual safety inspections and has a low personal property tax on vehicles.

south-dakota.name: South Dakota
south-dakota.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
south-dakota.lemonLawSummary: South Dakota's rights period in SDCL 32-6D-1 and 32-6D-5 is one year or 12,000 miles, and the problem has to start during that period. Repairs that count toward the presumption can run out to 24 months or 24,000 miles, so long as one attempt happened during the rights period. The test is four repairs plus a final attempt by the manufacturer, or 30 calendar days out of service with that final attempt included. Before a lawsuit, mail a certified demand to correct the problem; once the presumption is already met, the manufacturer has seven calendar days to designate a facility and 14 calendar days after the car arrives to finish the repair.
south-dakota.lemonLawCitation: SDCL 32-6D-5; lemon law rights period defined in SDCL 32-6D-1
south-dakota.registrationNotes: A noncommercial vehicle under 10 years old pays $36, $72, $108, or $144 for 12 months by weight. The same weight classes pay $25.20, $50.40, $75.60, or $100.80 once the vehicle is 10 years or older. The motor vehicle excise tax is 4 percent of the purchase price. Personal property is not taxable.
south-dakota.evRegistrationDetails: The fee list includes a $100 fee for an electric vehicle.
south-dakota.description: South Dakota requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections and has no state income tax.

tennessee.name: Tennessee
tennessee.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
tennessee.lemonLawSummary: Tenn. Code Ann. §§ 55-24-101(7) and 55-24-105 call the coverage a term of protection. It lasts for the express warranty or for one year after delivery, whichever finishes first, and miles do not shorten it. Inside that term, three repairs of the same problem or 30 calendar days out of service is the presumption. Send certified mail before you go further, and if the presumption is already met the manufacturer gets one more chance of not more than ten days.
tennessee.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is no longer required in Tennessee. The county clerk registration guide says the requirement ended in February 2022. Davidson County ended its program on February 5, 2022. EPA removed the inspection-and-maintenance programs for Davidson, Sumner, Rutherford, Williamson, Wilson, and Hamilton counties from the state plan.
tennessee.registrationNotes: State and local sales tax applies to a purchase.
tennessee.description: Tennessee requires liability insurance. Emissions testing is no longer required. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and charges no state income tax on wages.

texas.name: Texas
texas.insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
texas.lemonLawSummary: Tex. Occ. Code § 2301.605 sets the presumption before the express warranty expires or before 24 months or 24,000 miles, whichever comes first. The same nonconformity after four or more repairs is one path. A serious safety hazard after two or more repairs is the second path. A nonconformity that still substantially impairs use or market value after 30 or more cumulative days out of service is the third path. Subsection (b) extends those periods for war, invasion, strike, fire, flood, or another natural disaster, and subsection (c) leaves out any days the manufacturer or distributor lends a comparable vehicle while a franchised dealer repairs the owner's car. An order under § 2301.606(c) requires written notice of the defect and a chance for the manufacturer, converter, or distributor to cure.
texas.evIncentiveDetails: The 2026 Texas Light-Duty Motor Vehicle Purchase or Lease Incentive round for EVs is closed.
texas.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing applies to gasoline vehicles registered in Brazoria, Collin, Dallas, Denton, El Paso, Ellis, Fort Bend, Galveston, Harris, Johnson, Kaufman, Montgomery, Parker, Rockwall, Tarrant, Travis, and Williamson counties. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this test. Bexar County gasoline vehicles that are 2 to 24 model years old start emissions testing on November 1, 2026.
texas.safetyInspectionDetails: Personal-vehicle safety inspections ended on January 1, 2025, under HB 3297. Non-commercial vehicles pay a $7.50 inspection-program replacement fee at registration. A qualifying new passenger car or light truck pays $16.75 once, covering two years. Commercial vehicles still need a safety inspection and do not pay the replacement fee.
texas.registrationNotes: A 6.25 percent motor vehicle sales tax applies to purchases.
texas.description: Texas requires liability insurance. Personal-vehicle safety inspections ended on January 1, 2025. Registration includes a $7.50 inspection-program replacement fee, and emissions testing applies to gasoline vehicles in 17 counties.

utah.name: Utah
utah.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $65,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage / $3,000 PIP
utah.lemonLawSummary: Utah Code § 13-20-5 starts from the express warranty and from the first anniversary of delivery, and it uses whichever of those dates arrives sooner. The section does not limit the presumption by miles. A reasonable number of attempts is four tries at the same problem, or 30 business days the car is out for repair. Section 13-20-3 is the report rule: tell the manufacturer, its agent, or its authorized dealer during the warranty or during that same year.
utah.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing applies to many gasoline vehicles in Salt Lake, Davis, Utah, Weber, and Cache counties. Frequency depends on the county and the model year. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
utah.safetyInspectionDetails: Utah ended the safety-inspection requirement for most passenger vehicles on January 1, 2018. A safety inspection is still required for a rebuilt salvage title, a first-time street-legal ATV, and certain commercial vehicles and three-axle motor homes. It is not a prerequisite for ordinary passenger registration.
utah.registrationNotes: Utah Code 41-1a-1206 sets a $44 base for a motor vehicle of 14,000 pounds or less. A 2026 legislative fee brief is the source of the adjusted registration amount. The uniform fee is $150 for a passenger vehicle of model year 2024 through 2026, then $110, $80, $50, and $10 for older vehicles. That uniform fee is charged in addition to registration.
utah.plateFee: Set in the DMV fee schedule
utah.description: Utah requires liability insurance and emissions testing in Cache, Davis, Salt Lake, Utah, and Weber counties. A safety inspection is not required for most passenger vehicles.

vermont.name: Vermont
vermont.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
vermont.lemonLawSummary: Vermont's presumption in 9 V.S.A. § 4172(g) is tied to the express warranty, and at least the first repair attempt has to happen while that warranty is still in effect. Three repairs of the same problem, documented on written repair orders and generally at the same dealer, or 30 calendar days out of service, is the test. A car the owner can still drive for most of the day is not treated as out of service. After a reasonable repair attempt or after those 30 days, § 4173 says notify the manufacturer in writing and then choose arbitration; the manufacturer gets one final repair chance during the arbitration.
vermont.emissionsDetails: The emissions check is part of the annual inspection for a covered gasoline vehicle. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
vermont.safetyInspectionDetails: Every motor vehicle registered in Vermont must be inspected once each year. The inspection manual includes an OBD-II test for a vehicle 16 model years old or newer with a gross vehicle weight rating of 8,500 pounds or less. The station sets the inspection charge.
vermont.registrationNotes: A two-year gas or diesel registration is $167. A replacement plate is $15, and a set of two is $29. Purchase and use tax is 6 percent of the purchase price or the J.D. Power clean trade-in value, whichever is greater.
vermont.evRegistrationDetails: The one-year registration for an electric automobile is $178. A two-year electric registration is $341. Those DMV amounts include the clean air fund fee and the EV infrastructure fee.
vermont.description: Vermont requires liability insurance and annual safety and emissions inspections. The state follows California emissions standards and offers incentives for electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles.

virginia.name: Virginia
virginia.insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
virginia.lemonLawSummary: Virginia's lemon-law rights period in Va. Code §§ 59.1-207.11 and 59.1-207.13(B) is 18 months after delivery, with no mileage cap, and it can run longer if the manufacturer was notified and the problem is still unrepaired at the end. The presumption is three repairs of the same problem, one repair of a serious safety defect, or 30 calendar days out of service, unless the repairs could not be performed for reasons beyond the manufacturer's control. A serious safety defect means a life-threatening malfunction that interferes with ordinary control of the car or creates a risk of fire or explosion. Notify the manufacturer of the need for repair unless it was already notified, and if the presumption is already met the manufacturer gets up to 15 more days to correct it; the warranty or owner's manual has to disclose that written notification is required.
virginia.lemonLawCitation: Va. Code § 59.1-207.13(B); lemon law rights period defined in § 59.1-207.11
virginia.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is a separate biennial test. It is required in Arlington, Fairfax, Loudoun, Prince William, and Stafford counties and in the cities of Alexandria, Fairfax, Falls Church, Manassas, and Manassas Park. A new vehicle is exempt for four years. The maximum fee is $30 under Va. Code § 46.2-1182. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
virginia.safetyInspectionDetails: An annual safety inspection is required statewide. A station may charge no more than $20 for a non-commercial vehicle, and the charge is not mandatory. The safety inspection does not include the emissions test.
virginia.registrationFeeRange: $30.75 at 4,000 lb or less, or $35.75 from 4,001 to 6,500 lb
virginia.registrationNotes: Registration adds $2 when the vehicle is garaged in a locality that requires the emissions test. The locality assesses personal property tax, and partial state relief is available.
virginia.evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays a highway use fee of $135.63. The Virginia DMV chart sets that annual amount for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
virginia.description: Virginia requires liability insurance and annual safety inspections statewide. The state has emissions testing in Northern Virginia and has a lemon law protecting new vehicle buyers.

washington.name: Washington
washington.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
washington.lemonLawSummary: Washington sets eligibility in RCW 19.118.021(6) at two years or 24,000 miles, and the written warranty used for the presumption in RCW 19.118.041(2) is at least one year or 12,000 miles. For a car that is not a motor home, the presumption is two repairs of the same serious safety defect, two or more different serious safety defects each repaired at least once within a 12-month period, four repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service with at least 15 of those days during the written warranty. A motor home uses one serious-safety repair plus a final attempt, three repairs plus a final attempt, or 60 days out of service. Make a written request to the manufacturer before a replacement or repurchase; a motor-home owner sends written notice so the manufacturers can make one last coordinated attempt after one serious-safety repair, three attempts, or 30 days out.
washington.lemonLawCitation: RCW 19.118.041(2); eligibility period defined in RCW 19.118.021(6)
washington.evIncentiveDetails: Washington's EV sales tax exemption expired July 31, 2025, and its instant EV rebate funding is fully claimed; a new program is expected in 2027.
washington.emissionsDetails: Washington's emission-check program ended on January 1, 2020. Vehicle owners no longer need an emissions test to renew registration. The Department of Ecology repealed the obsolete testing rules in 2021. Driving a vehicle with modified emissions equipment, or a vehicle that smokes, is still illegal.
washington.registrationNotes: Passenger vehicles also pay a $10 weight fee. A plate transfer is $10. Filing and service fees are charged in addition to the license tab. Inside the Sound Transit district, the RTA excise tax is 1.1 percent of depreciated value.
washington.evRegistrationDetails: At annual renewal, DOL lists an electric-car fee of $100, an electric-car fee of $50, and a transportation electrification fee of $75. Together those renewal fees are $225.
washington.description: Washington requires liability insurance. The state emission-check program ended on January 1, 2020, so registration no longer depends on an emissions test. Washington has no income tax, a strong lemon law, and had incentives for electric vehicles.

west-virginia.name: West Virginia
west-virginia.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
west-virginia.lemonLawSummary: The presumption in W. Va. Code § 46A-6A-5 stops at the end of the express warranty or at one year after delivery, whichever date is sooner. Miles do not limit it. A different clock, the repair duty in § 46A-6A-3, runs for the longer of those two periods. Three repairs of the same problem, 30 calendar days out of service, or one unsuccessful repair of a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, meets the presumption, but only after written notice and at least one chance to cure.
west-virginia.safetyInspectionDetails: West Virginia requires a safety inspection every 24 months under W. Va. Code § 17C-16-4, effective January 1, 2024. The maximum sticker fee is $19 for that two-year period. The inspection covers brakes, steering, tires, lights, glass, exhaust, horn, and mirrors.
west-virginia.registrationNotes: A 6 percent sales tax applies to a purchase. Personal property tax is also assessed.
west-virginia.description: West Virginia requires liability insurance and a safety inspection every 24 months. The state does not require emissions testing.

wisconsin.name: Wisconsin
wisconsin.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
wisconsin.lemonLawSummary: Wis. Stat. § 218.0171(1)(h) starts the clock at the end of the express warranty or one year after the first delivery, whichever happens sooner, and miles are not part of the test. Four repairs of the same problem, or 30 days out of service because of warranty problems, is a reasonable attempt to repair, and time lost to a flood, other natural disaster, war, invasion, fire, or strike does not count. A car the owner is still driving counts as out of service only when a problem substantially affects use or safety and has already had at least two repair attempts. After a reasonable attempt fails, give the manufacturer the form described in the statute before it has to refund or replace the car.
wisconsin.registrationNotes: A wheel tax may apply where the vehicle is kept. A hybrid electric automobile or light truck at or below 8,000 pounds pays a $75 surcharge.
wisconsin.evRegistrationDetails: An electric automobile or light truck at or below 8,000 pounds pays a $175 surcharge.
wisconsin.description: Wisconsin requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections for most personal vehicles.

wyoming.name: Wyoming
wyoming.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
wyoming.lemonLawSummary: Wyoming's lemon law, Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 40-17-101, places the repair duty and the presumption within one year after delivery. More than three repairs of the same problem, or 30 business days out of service, is the presumption. During that year, tell the manufacturer, its agent, or the dealer authorized to do the repair. The refund or replacement remedy is withheld if the owner has not finished a manufacturer's informal dispute program that meets federal rules.
wyoming.registrationFeeRange: $30 state fee plus a county fee
wyoming.registrationNotes: The county fee is 3 percent of a declining share of factory price, with a $5 minimum. A replacement plate after loss is $8.
wyoming.description: Wyoming requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections and has no state income tax.

washington-dc.name: Washington DC
washington-dc.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
washington-dc.lemonLawSummary: D.C. Code § 50-502(d) uses the first 18,000 miles or two years after delivery to the original purchaser. Four repairs of a non-safety problem, one repair of a safety-related problem, or 30 days out of service, is the presumption, and those 30 days can be extended for a war, invasion, strike, fire, flood, or similar disaster. While that window is open, tell the manufacturer, an agent, or an authorized dealer, and if the agent or dealer is the one who receives it, that person has seven days to forward certified mail to the manufacturer. A lawsuit waits until the claim has been submitted to the Board of Consumer Claims Arbitration under § 50-503.
washington-dc.emissionsDetails: Private passenger vehicles need an emissions inspection every two years. The inspection fee is $35. A fully electric passenger vehicle can receive a non-expiring inspection sticker. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
washington-dc.safetyInspectionDetails: Private passenger vehicles in the District of Columbia do not take a safety inspection.
washington-dc.registrationNotes: Those passenger amounts took effect on March 30, 2026. Regular tag replacement is $15. A hybrid does not qualify for the battery-electric registration rate.
washington-dc.description: Washington DC has some of the most comprehensive vehicle ownership regulations in the nation. As the nation's capital, DC requires liability insurance, annual vehicle inspections, and offers generous incentives for electric vehicle adoption as part of its sustainability goals.
